  In this work, we propose a user-centric evaluation framework based on large language models (LLMs) for CRSs, namely Conversational Recommendation Evaluator (CoRE). CoRE consists of two main components: (1) LLM-As-Evaluator. Firstly, we comprehensively summarize 12 key factors influencing user experience in CRSs and directly leverage LLM as an evaluator to assign a score to each factor. (2) Multi-Agent Debater. Secondly, we design a multi-agent debate framework with four distinct roles (common user, domain expert, linguist, and HCI expert) to discuss and synthesize the 12 evaluation factors into a unified overall performance score.
  Furthermore, we apply the proposed framework to evaluate four CRSs on two benchmark datasets. The experimental results show that CoRE aligns well with human evaluation in most of the 12 factors and the overall assessment. Especially, CoRE's overall evaluation scores demonstrate significantly better alignment with human feedback compared to existing rule-based metrics.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A search agent can leave an earlier error unresolved by missing the right source, overlooking a relevant passage, or failing to revise and deliver the answer after receiving the evidence. We evaluate these possibilities on BrowseComp-Plus by replaying each model's own wrong closed-book answer in conversation and intervening on what evidence reaches the model. In a supplied-evidence study spanning four open-weight checkpoints, 709 questions and 26,665 test conditions, a confident assistant prior reduced Nemotron's paired accuracy by 16.1 percentage points despite answer-bearing passages in context. When the user insisted on the prior, accuracy fell by 32.9 points for Nemotron and 12.6 for gpt-oss. Among gpt-oss responses that lost correctness in that condition, abstention was more common than repeating the prior. In separate search interventions with Qwen3.5 and Nemotron, placing a gold page first often left the decisive source unopened. Delivering a decisive passage in context improved accuracy over neutral delivery by 51.0 percentage points for Qwen3.5 and 22.4 for Nemotron. Even with the passage in context, Nemotron exhausted its search budget and returned no answer in 19 of 51 episodes. The tests distinguish failures of retrieval, passage delivery, correction and answer completion, giving system builders a way to test which changes resolve a recurring error.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Healthcare systems continually revise clinical taxonomies, update reimbursement schedules, and harmonize cross-border registries. Existing automated coding models bind clinical text understanding to fixed vocabulary-specific heads, requiring manual relabeling and retraining whenever code sets change. We introduce Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields (OCSF), a vocabulary-free framework that decouples clinical document reading from target ontology indexing so one trained encoder can switch across arbitrary medical vocabularies in seconds without target training. A single-pass bidirectional diffusion-pretrained encoder and vocabulary-free decoder map each clinical note into a fixed-dimension two-dimensional state matrix with zero code-specific parameters. Any target ontology is compiled offline on CPU from public text descriptions into a scale-invariant Tikhonov deconvolution operator that suppresses sibling-code interference while preserving source decision thresholds. Trained solely on English MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharge summaries and evaluated without target tuning across 58,706 held-out test notes and five unseen ontologies spanning English ICD-10, MS-DRG, Spanish, Greek, and Chinese (115-185,458 codes), OCSF reaches 63.15% Micro-F1 on in-domain ICD-9 (outperforming a matched closed-vocabulary classifier and eliminating late-epoch tail overfitting) and transfers directly to 26,085 English ICD-10 codes (29.23% recall at gold cardinality), MS-DRG groups, and multilingual terminologies, compiling up to 185,458 codes in under 10 seconds on CPU with sub-millisecond GPU readout.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 21 pages, 4 figures, 4 main tables, 5 supplementary tables. Code available at https://github.com/ZeqiangWangAI/OCSF

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Beyond Knowledge Transfer: How User Overlap Shapes Diversity in Cross-Domain Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A common paradigm in cross-domain recommendation (CDR) transfers knowledge through users shared by source and target domains. Although this overlap bridge is effective in improving accuracy, its effect on diversity remains unclear. We identify two bottlenecks: the bridge can be too narrow when overlapping users cover limited target-domain tastes, and too loud when shared signals dominate the sparse personal evidence of non-overlapping users. To address both, we propose DivCDR, a model-agnostic Push--Pull framework. Pull constructs confidence-gated virtual positives for overlapping users and optimizes their exposure-entropy gain, broadening the preferences carried by the bridge. Push uses overlap-density-guided negative sampling to move non-overlapping users away from overlap-dense regions. Experiments on three datasets and five representative CDR backbones show that DivCDR improves recommendation diversity while preserving or improving accuracy in most settings.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Transform Before You Query: A Privacy-Preserving Approach for Vector Retrieval with Embedding Space Alignment
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Vector Database (VDB) can efficiently index and search high-dimensional vector embeddings from unstructured data, crucially enabling fast semantic similarity search essential for modern AI applications like generative AI and recommendation systems. Since current VDB service providers predominantly use proprietary black-box models, users are forced to expose raw query text to them via API in exchange for the vector retrieval services. Consequently, if query text involves confidential records from finance or healthcare domains, this mechanism inevitably leads to critical leakage of user's sensitive information. To address this issue, we introduce STEER (\textbf{S}ecure \textbf{T}ransformed \textbf{E}mbedding v\textbf{E}ctor\textbf{ R}etrieval), a private vector retrieval framework that leverages the alignment relationship between the semantic spaces of different embedding models to derive approximate embeddings for the query text. STEER performs the retrieval using the approximate embeddings within the original VDB and requires no modifications to the server side. Our theoretical and experimental analyses demonstrate that STEER effectively safeguards query text privacy while maintaining the retrieval accuracy. Even though approximate embeddings are approximations of the embeddings from proprietary models, they still prevent the providers from recovering the query text through Embedding Inversion Attacks (EIAs). Extensive experimental results show that Recall@100 of STEER can basically achieve a decrease of less than 5\%. Furthermore, even when searching within a text corpus of millions of entries, STEER achieves a Recall@20 accuracy 20\% higher than current baselines.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Multimodal embedding models map heterogeneous inputs into a shared representation space, yet text-only, image-only, and composed inputs are still presented in distinct formats and follow different routes through the model. This fragmentation prevents heterogeneous tasks from jointly optimizing the same end-to-end encoding process, limiting supervision transfer across input configurations. To address this issue, we propose unification before encoding and instantiate this paradigm in RenderEmbed. The framework uses Visual Substrate Rendering to convert heterogeneous inputs into a common visual substrate for encoding with a VLM. From the resulting visual tokens, Progressive Hierarchical Anchor Encoding produces compact retrieval representations by interleaving learnable anchors and fusing their states across layers, retaining broad context and fine-grained cues. Interventional Rendering Learning trains these representations to remain sensitive to content changes and stable across rendering variations through complementary semantic and rendering interventions. Extensive experiments on MMEB and ViDoRe v2, spanning diverse retrieval tasks, show that RenderEmbed outperforms prior state-of-the-art models at the same scale and exhibits strong out-of-domain generalization. Compared with MetaEmbed, RenderEmbed improves MMEB Overall Precision@1 by 1.7 points, with a larger 2.1-point gain on out-of-domain tasks. Transfer and scaling analyses further show that a shared visual pathway enables more effective learning from heterogeneous supervision.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A tool router retrieves a few candidate tools per request and lets a language model choose. Methods that share experience across organizations add past requests about each tool to what the router retrieves. StableToolBench calls some of its test groups tests on "unseen" tools, yet the ToolBench instruction pool, which retrievers and experience-sharing methods learn from, contains every test query and labels every gold tool of the two single-tool groups among them. We release STUN-Bench (StableToolBench, Truly UNseen), a split whose experience pool has no item that labels or names 172 held-out tools. Unseen here means absent from shared experience and retriever training data, not from pretraining. On the split we find crowding: experience pooled from five simulated clients, added to an index of tool descriptions, outranks the descriptions of tools no client has used, which then often drop out of the candidate list. Under the Jina-v2 retriever, routing accuracy on held-out tools falls from 0.534 to 0.278. Retrievers trained for tool retrieval lose much less, and keeping experience in a separate index recovers most of the loss under Jina-v2. The split also reverses a conclusion: with every test tool labeled in the pool and our default leak filter applied, shared experience beats descriptions alone; on STUN-Bench it falls below them. The split, leak filter and evaluation harness are available at https://github.com/<org>/STUN-Bench.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Large language models (LLMs) answer many diet and health questions but can state unsupported claims and cite sources that do not support them. We present SHAKTI (Smart Health Advisor for Knowledge-based Tailored Interventions), a conversational assistant that answers only from retrieved scholarly papers and exact food-composition data, and evaluate it with retrieval, generation, grounding, efficiency and contextawareness metrics. We indexed 484,368,086 OpenAlex works, searched exactly on a GPU for evaluation (10,065 NFCorpus, BioASQ, SciFact and PubMedQA questions) and through a compressed 230-million-abstract index in deployment. On 1,000 stratified questions, we compared single-shot, multi-hop, corrective and deep-research retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Claude Sonnet. SHAKTI adds conversational query rewriting, USDA FoodData Central lookups, source-link checks and online verification of quotes and numbers. It was tested in 36 scripted conversational turns, a 248-question memory-depth test and a 38-question load test. Claims were checked by a Claude Opus judge against exactly the text the system saw. MedCPT reranking of hybrid retrieval gave the best MRR (0.21) and MAP@100 (0.14). Across existing RAG methods, faithfulness was 0.95-0.96, claim hallucination 0.5-0.8% and context precision up to 0.98; the deep-research agent answered 73.2% of BioASQ questions correctly. In conversation, SHAKTI reached a context-awareness score of 97.1%, faithfulness 95.5%, 1.9% unsupported claims, no contradicted claims and 229/229 working source links; it resolved references to the first question after 16 unrelated questions. An answer cost 14,716 tokens (US$0.06) with a median latency of 24 s. Large-scale retrieval with agentic evidence selection and mechanical verification yields auditable, low-hallucination nutrition answers.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: EcoGEO: Trajectory-Aware Evidence Ecosystems for Web-Enabled LLM Search Agents
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Web-enabled LLM agents are changing how online information influences search outcomes. Existing Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) studies mainly focus on individual webpages. However, agentic web search is not a single-document setting: an agent may issue queries, crawl pages, follow links, reformulate searches, and synthesize evidence across multiple browsing steps. Influence therefore depends not only on page content, but also on how pages are organized, connected, and encountered along the agent's browsing trajectory. We study this shift through Ecosystem Generative Engine Optimization (EcoGEO), which treats GEO as an environment-level influence problem for web-enabled LLM agents. To instantiate this perspective, we propose TRACE, a Trajectory-Aware Coordinated Evidence Ecosystem. Given a recommendation query and a fictional target product, our method builds a controlled evidence environment that coordinates an agent-facing navigation entry page with heterogeneous support pages. These pages use shared terminology, internal links, and consistent product attributes to introduce, verify, and reinforce the target product. We evaluate our method on OPR-Bench, a benchmark for open-ended product recommendation. Experiments show that it consistently outperforms page-level GEO baselines in Recommendation. Trajectory-level metrics show improved initial target access and additional internal-link browsing, while follow-up-search effects vary across backbones and comparison methods. Together with the multi-page baseline and ablations, these findings support the role of evidence organization in shaping the agent's evidence-acquisition process. Overall, our findings support an ecosystem research paradigm for GEO, where web-enabled LLM agents are studied in relation to the broader evidence environments that guide search, browsing, and answer synthesis.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Dataset available at: https://github.com/BoBo-Ye/EcoGEO

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered dense search, and (iii) expands top passages into contiguous, section-aware spans under a token budget, plus content-hash-gated delta ingestion to keep the index cheap to update. We evaluate on five public-domain books (113 chapter-localization queries) and on QuALITY and NovelQA (200K+ token novels). In-house, we find a seed-stable precision/ranking tradeoff: with section expansion off, hierarchical retrieval returns a higher fraction of chunks from the correct chapter (+3.3pp, Wilcoxon p=0.014); with expansion on, ranking improves (MRR, p=0.040). Accuracy differences are not significant. On QuALITY, hierarchical retrieval beats flat top-k (81.0% vs 70.4%, p=0.0019) and matches the full article (p=0.74). On NovelQA, hierarchical and flat retrieval are statistically tied (55.7% vs 56.8%, p=0.24); hierarchy helps aggregation questions while flat wins on localized facts. Against a faithful RAPTOR baseline we find a complementary tradeoff, not superiority. Delta ingestion reuses 94 to 99.7% of embeddings on incremental edits. We make no claim of semantic chapter-boundary inference and scope claims to English narrative prose.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: UniFAR: A Unified Facet-Aware Retrieval Framework for Scientific Documents
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Scientific document retrieval (SDR) plays a critical role in modern scientific research, supporting knowledge discovery and evidence-based reasoning. It has evolved along two paradigms: document--document (doc-doc) retrieval driven by inter-document contrastive learning, and question--document (q-doc) retrieval emerging from LLMs and RAG for natural-language interaction. In practice, scientific workflows rely on both paradigms, requiring the retrieval of related papers given a seed document and identifying relevant documents given a user question. However, existing methods typically treat two paradigms separately, hindering their complementary strengths. To address this, we propose UniFAR, a unified facet-aware retrieval framework that jointly supports both doc-doc and q-doc retrieval within a shared representation space. UniFAR introduces a multi-granularity representation and aggregation module to unify the encoding of scientific papers and natural-language questions, and a facet-level modeling mechanism with learnable anchors to produce representations for three interpretable semantic facets---background, method and result. A facet-aware joint training strategy is further proposed to integrate doc-doc and q-doc contrastive objectives with sentence-level facet alignment, enabling unified learning from both inter-document relations and question-oriented supervision. Experiments on five benchmarks spanning computer science, medicine, and biology demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of UniFAR in both doc-doc and q-doc retrieval tasks and across multiple backbone models.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Look Before You Leap: Re-Architecting Disk-Resident Vector Search with TriVS
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary:
Disk-resident approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) scales vector search beyond DRAM, yet state-of-the-art systems remain I/O-bound, even with fast SSDs and sophisticated I/O execution. To understand this bottleneck, we conduct an I/O-centric analysis that breaks each query down into an approach phase that locates a query-near region and a converge phase that resolves the final top-k. This analysis reveals complementary I/O tradeoffs: cluster-based search circumvents approach-phase I/O through in-memory routing but reads coarse-grained, full clusters during convergence, whereas graph-based search employs fine-grained, vector-level I/O throughout, enabling efficient convergence at the cost of inevitable I/O during the approach phase.
  To combine the complementary I/O benefits of the two granularities, we present TriVS, a new paradigm that re-architects disk-resident vector search as a trilogy: approach coarsely, distill progressively, and converge exactly. Its key innovations come in two parts. First, it decouples the approach and converge phases from a single search granularity, employing cluster-based search to avoid approach-phase I/O and leveraging vector-level I/O for efficient convergence. Second, to bridge the two granularities, it introduces a new in-memory distill phase between the original two, progressively reducing routed clusters to a vector-level shortlist using compact quantized vectors before disk access. Moreover, coarser clustering shrinks the centroid-routing index, allowing TriVS to reallocate existing memory to distillation rather than expand its memory budget. Our evaluation on five datasets spanning diverse vector types and scales shows that, at Recall@10=0.9, TriVS achieves on average 3.42X PipeANN's throughput, 51.2% lower latency, and 63.7% less disk I/O, while using less memory and storage than PipeANN.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Perfect Clustering in Extremely Sparse Multilayer Networks with Groupwise Subspace Structure
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: The paper studies a multilayer network on the same collection of nodes, where each layer follows the Generalized Random Dot Product Graph Model. Furthermore, all layers can be partitioned into groups, each group with its own unique latent subspace structure, but otherwise the matrices of connection probabilities can all be different. This setting is extremely general and includes most multilayer network models as special cases. In addition, we are interested in the situation where the layer networks may be extremely sparse and, therefore, the layer-by-layer analysis is unreliable. This problem can also be seen as a generalization of the classic setting in which one recovers a shared structure across an entire collection of matrices, extending it to the case where such structures are shared only within specific groups of matrices. The key task in this setting is to recover the groups of layers with unique subspace structures, since, after that, the information in those groups of layers can be pooled together by well-studied methods. Until now, clustering of layers in such networks was based on layer-by-layer analysis, which required the multilayer network to be sufficiently dense. Our paper is the first to provide a tensor-based approach to the problem that combines information from all layers in an unconventional manner. Our theoretical results, established under intuitive and non-restrictive assumptions, assert that the new technique achieves perfect clustering under sparsity conditions that, up to logarithmic factors, coincide with the computational lower bound derived for a much simpler model. The paper also delivers a nuanced message about the applicability of the new technique.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Flexible Matrix Estimation with Side Information
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We introduce a flexible framework for high-dimensional matrix estimation to incorporate side information for both rows and columns. Existing approaches, such as inductive matrix completion, often impose restrictive structure---for example, an exact low-rank covariate interaction term, linear covariate effects, and limited ability to exploit components explained only by one side (row or column) or by neither---and frequently omit an explicit noise component. To address these limitations, we propose to decompose the underlying matrix as the sum of four complementary components: (possibly nonlinear) interaction between row and column characteristics; row characteristic-driven component, column characteristic-driven component, and residual low-rank structure unexplained by observed characteristics. By combining sieve-based projection with nuclear-norm penalization, each component can be estimated separately and these estimated components can then be aggregated to yield a final estimate. We derive Frobenius- and entrywise-norm convergence rates that demonstrate the robustness of our estimator across a broad range of model configurations with varying degrees of informativeness in the side information. We further extend the method to partially observed matrices under both missing-at-random and missing-not-at-random mechanisms, including block-missing patterns motivated by causal panel data. Simulations and a real-data application to tobacco sales show that leveraging side information improves imputation accuracy and can enhance treatment-effect estimation relative to standard low-rank and spectral-based alternatives.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Causal pieces: analysing and improving spiking neural networks piece by piece
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We introduce "causal pieces", a novel concept for analysing spiking neural networks (SNNs), inspired by "linear pieces" used to study expressivity and trainability in artificial neural networks (ANNs). Causal pieces partition the input and parameter space of a feedforward SNN with single-spike coding into distinct regions where the same subnetwork causes the output spikes. For networks of current-based leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons with large membrane time constants, we show that within each causal piece, output spike times are locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to inputs and network parameters. We further prove a lower bound on the approximation error that depends on the number of causal pieces. Thus, the number of causal pieces is a measure of the approximation capabilities of SNNs, which is valid despite spike-time discontinuities and applies to networks with both excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Empirically, we find that parameter initialisations yielding more causal pieces on the training set strongly correlate with SNN training success across multiple benchmarks, including Yin-Yang, Fashion-MNIST, and EuroSAT. Moreover, simulations with standard single-spike LIF neurons indicate that our findings extend beyond the theoretically analysed regime. These results establish causal pieces as a powerful and principled tool for analysing and improving the computational capabilities of SNNs.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Sequential Monte Carlo approximations of Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We consider the problem of sampling from a probability distribution $π$. It is well known that this can be written as an optimisation problem over the space of probability distribution in which we aim to minimise the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $π$. We consider several partial differential equations (PDEs) whose solution is a minimiser of the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $π$ and connect them to well-known Monte Carlo algorithms. We focus in particular on PDEs obtained by considering the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao geometry over the space of probabilities and show that these lead to a natural implementation using importance sampling and sequential Monte Carlo. We propose a novel algorithm to approximate the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao flow of the Kullback--Leibler divergence and conduct an extensive empirical study to identify when this algorithm outperforms other popular Monte Carlo algorithms.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: Changes from v1: the study of tempered dynamics was removed in favour of a larger experimental section

Statistical Machine Learning.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nyström approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Bayesian Data Integration and Model Updating in Probabilistic Digital Twins
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: This paper proposes a framework for sequential Bayesian updating in probabilistic digital twins using data from multiple sources collected over time. The framework distinguishes between property data and behavior data, according to how observations relate to the digital state. Property data directly inform a subset of the uncertain model parameters and can therefore be incorporated using efficient dedicated Bayesian updating methods. Behavior data provide indirect information through the prediction model and require the solution of a Bayesian inverse problem. To reduce the associated computational cost, an active-learning-based surrogate strategy is introduced that evolves with the digital state and adaptively refines the prediction model in regions relevant to posterior inference. The framework is evaluated using an idealized cantilever beam example and a geotechnical case study of a canal wall subject to varying water levels and corrosion. The examples show how complementary data sources, including both equality observations and inequality information from observed system survival, can inform uncertain parameters and system reliability. The proposed surrogate-based updating scheme yields posterior estimates and prediction accuracy comparable to those of physics-based updating while requiring substantially fewer model evaluations. The proposed framework thus supports multi-source updating and reliability assessment in probabilistic digital twins of engineering systems.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Generalized Guarantees for Variational Inference in the Presence of Even and Elliptical Symmetry
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Variational inference (VI) approximates a target density $p$ by the best match $q$ in a family $\mathcal Q$ of tractable distributions. The variational approximation is found by minimizing a divergence, most commonly the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence $\text{KL}(q||p)$, although other divergences can be considered. In practice, $p \notin \mathcal Q$ and so the optimal variational approximation is misspecified. Despite this misspecification, it was recently shown that the minimizer of $\text{KL}(q||p)$ is guaranteed to recover the mean in the presence of even symmetry and likewise the correlation matrix in the presence of elliptical symmetry for a log-concave target $p$. We extend this result in several directions. First, we relax the assumption of log-concavity and instead merely require $p$ to be unimodal, allowing for heavy-tailed targets. Second, we obtain guarantees for cases where $p$ exhibits symmetry along some but not all of its coordinates. These partial symmetries arise naturally in Bayesian hierarchical models, where the prior induces a challenging geometry but still possesses axes of symmetry. Third, we extend these guarantees to $f$-divergences, a broad class which includes the forward and reverse-KL divergences and the $α$-divergences.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Instance-Dependent Bandit Convex Optimization in One Dimension
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study the instance-dependent sample complexity of one-dimensional stochastic bandit convex optimization in the fixed-confidence setting. First, we consider minimizer localization, where the learner seeks to identify a point within distance $\varepsilon$ of the unique minimizer. We introduce a new instance-dependent quantity $Δ_\varepsilon(f)$, corresponding to the threshold for which the sublevel set of $f-\min f$ has length $2\varepsilon$. We prove a lower bound of order $Δ_\varepsilon(f)^{-2}$ and give a bisection-style algorithm that matches this rate up to logarithmic factors. We then revisit the simple-regret setting, where the goal is to identify an $\varepsilon$-optimal point. Surprisingly, no comparable instance-dependent improvement is possible: every correct algorithm has sample complexity of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ on every instance, matching the minimax rate up to constants. Together, these results separate the statistical complexity of minimizer localization from that of simple-regret optimization in one-dimensional convex bandits.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: ExitLUT: Boolean Early Exits for Efficient FPGA-Based Neural Network Inference
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Early exit neural networks reduce average inference cost by terminating once sufficient confidence is reached. On FPGAs, conventional confidence-based exits add arithmetic control paths poorly matched to LUT fabrics, consuming resources that could otherwise support the main datapath. We present ExitLUT, which replaces softmax-style exit decisions with learned Boolean functions mapped directly into FPGA LUTs. In our CNN evaluation, fpgaConvNet is the static spatial-dataflow baseline, while ATHEENA is its softmax-based early exit extension. ExitLUT reduces ATHEENA's exit-decision LUT usage by 2.58$\times$ over the softmax path and eliminates decision-path DSP usage, while preserving accuracy and exit behavior. Rerunning design-space exploration reinvests these savings into the datapath, improving throughput by up to 4.08$\times$ over fpgaConvNet and 1.82$\times$ over ATHEENA. For LUT-based NNs, embedded ExitLUT exits achieve 1.41-1.89$\times$ average time-to-decision speedup over static NeuraLUT-Assemble designs with under 1% LUT overhead.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures. Accepted to the 2026 International Conference on Field Programmable Technology (ICFPT)

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for mappings between function spaces, but their reliability cannot be characterized by the performance of a single trained model. Existing neural operator uncertainty quantification approaches often characterize predictive uncertainty without separately identifying the contributions of individual sources of epistemic uncertainty. Finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization can produce substantial variation among learned operators even when the underlying physical problem is deterministic. We systematically investigate these sources of epistemic uncertainty across a diverse set of operator learning architectures. Across our experiments, we train approximately 46,000 neural operator models and construct ensembles over training datasets, model initializations, and output discretizations to characterize distributions of relative $L_2$ error rather than individual trained realizations. We find substantial architecture-dependent differences in epistemic uncertainty, with model initialization often accounting for the largest proportion of variance in relative $L_2$ error. The ranked performance of neural operator architectures can invert as the number and spatial distribution of output samples change, with the best architectures under sparse or randomly sampled observations differing from those at higher-resolution or structured discretizations. Furthermore, ensembles that reliably characterize aggregate operator error can provide unreliable estimates of error quantiles for individual test functions. These results highlight the importance of distinguishing the sources of epistemic uncertainty when evaluating neural operator reliability and establishing robust benchmarking practices.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UEA regular multivariate time series benchmarks specifically when class-discriminative information is purely geometric.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Transformers with Signatures: Towards Universal In-Context Learning in Path Space
Statistical Machine Learning.summary:
In-context learning (ICL) enables transformers to adapt to new tasks from demonstrations without updating their parameters. However, theoretical guarantees for transformers remain limited in general, and elusive in particular when target responses depend nonlinearly on the evolution of observed paths. We establish an ICL framework for path space, using path signature features. Building on the universal linear approximation property of signatures, we construct explicitly a causal softmax transformer with two attention heads per layer that emulates in-context Lasso. Under sparse signature approximation and suitable moment and concentration conditions, we establish finite-sample prediction error bounds. Our analysis goes beyond the IID data setting in the existing ICL theory, allowing dependence among demonstrations and the query.
  Experiments on in-context sparse recovery, nonlinear path regression, execution-cost prediction, and financial payoff inference demonstrate robustness to changes in observation grids and adaptation to unseen market environments. Across these prediction tasks, transformers with signatures match or outperform vanilla transformer baselines with substantially fewer trainable parameters, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of signature-based ICL.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Efficient Cost-Aware LLM Evaluation via Bayesian Bandit Gittins Indices
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Exhaustively evaluating every candidate LLM configuration on every benchmark item to identify a high-performing one is costly. We formulate configuration selection as a cost-aware Bayesian bandit problem and propose GittinsEval, inspired by Bayesian-optimal Gittins-index policies for Markov chain selection. We augment this policy with a separate anytime recommendation rule over both fully and partially evaluated configurations, using an LCB-style score to account for posterior uncertainty. GittinsEval is computationally efficient, requiring only lightweight online updates after offline precomputation. Across tasks with varying numbers of candidates and examples, GittinsEval is consistently competitive, with particularly strong gains over the Bayesian optimization baselines on few-candidate large-example benchmarks and over cost-unaware frequentist baselines on large-candidate tasks. Crucially, GittinsEval often attains near-zero simple regret using only 1%-2% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost; it also offers a stopping rule that typically triggers at 1%-10% with an appropriate cost--quality tradeoff parameter.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: Spotlight at ICML 2026 Workshop on Decision-Making from Offline Datasets to Online Adaptation: Black-Box Optimization to Reinforcement Learning (DEMO)

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. After each batch, CC-Gittins recommends assignments that are nondominated under uncertainty-adjusted estimates of quality and deployment cost. We evaluate CC-Gittins on eight quality--cost matrices from workflows with two to five roles and up to 1,681 candidate assignments. We also evaluate the method with latency as a third objective. Across the eight benchmarks, CC-Gittins recovers a substantial fraction of the true Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost, and recovers most of the frontier with few false positives by 30%.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: Preliminary version accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Resource-Aware Agentic AI (RAAAI)

Statistical Machine Learning.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a single-player deck-building game that requires long-term planning under heavy randomness. We present AlphaDefect, an expert-level AI system for STS2: for each character, one network trained with proximal policy optimization (PPO) makes every decision of a run, in combat and outside it. At the highest difficulty, Ascension 10, on two versions of the game current in November 2026 and on test seeds not played in training, AlphaDefect wins 62-77% of runs across six characters with greedy play and 68-80% with test-time search, after 1.3 to 6.7 billion decisions of training per character; runs uploaded by human players of all levels are won 11-20% of the time at the same difficulty. The networks read the game as entity records that identify each card, relic and enemy through a learned embedding and attributes from the game data, together with consequences of public information computed by the engine. Ablations show how much the agent depends on this encoding: without these identities, the network did not win a single run, and without the computed consequences it won 8.3 points fewer. To our knowledge, AlphaDefect is the strongest publicly reported STS2 agent as of November 2026.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Multimodal tabular learning combines tabular data with images and text, often in settings where labeled data are scarce. Tabular foundation models such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) offer a promising solution via in-context learning without task-specific training. However, modern image and text encoders produce embeddings with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, far exceeding the number of features encountered during PFN pretraining. Existing approaches bridge this gap using principal component analysis (PCA) to compress frozen embeddings. Surprisingly, we find that this PCA interface can underperform simple linear classifiers when labeled examples are scarce, even though PFNs are designed for small datasets. We identify the underlying failure mechanism: the PFN's per-column standardization removes the variances of the PCA scores. When the PCA keeps every direction of the labeled examples, the examples collapse into a regular simplex in which all pairwise distances are equal. To address this problem, we propose Rotated Frozen Embeddings (RoFE), a training-free method that rotates PCA scores before PFN inference. We theoretically show that rotation makes the column variances nearly equal, so that standardization approximately preserves the embedding geometry. Across image and text classification tasks, encoders, and tabular foundation models, RoFE improves low-data performance over the PCA interface and outperforms baselines that require task-specific training. The improvements also extend to regression.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
Statistical Machine Learning.summary:
Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist.
  On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions. This success has spurred substantial interest in using pretrained diffusion models as expressive priors for highly ill-posed inverse problems in imaging and sensing. Despite strong empirical performance, theoretical understanding of this approach remains limited: existing guarantees are often asymptotic or entail prohibitive computational costs in the worst case. In this paper, we address this gap by studying sparse recovery from a small number of linear measurements, a classical problem in compressed sensing. We show that, given an accurate diffusion model capturing a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior, a likelihood-guided annealed Langevin sampler provably recovers the sparse signal in polynomial time with near-optimal sample complexity for a broad family of random and deterministic sensing matrices. When the signal is indeed drawn from the postulated prior, we further establish total variation guarantees for posterior sampling after a final denoising step. These results lay a theoretical foundation for statistically and computationally efficient inverse solvers with diffusion priors.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Prediction-Powered Regression via Calibration: Beyond the Supervised Minimax Benchmark
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study nonparametric regression with limited labeled data and abundant observations carrying potentially inaccurate pseudo-labels. Our proposed method, weighted prediction-powered regression via calibration (wPPRC), first calibrates pseudo-labels using labeled data, then fits a predictor by weighted regression using observed and calibrated responses. Over Hölder classes, we derive nonasymptotic excess-risk bounds for clipped ReLU estimators and establish a minimax lower bound for the corresponding regression problem. Under suitable conditions, the upper and lower bounds match up to logarithmic factors. Moreover, wPPRC can achieve a worst-case risk of smaller order than the minimax risks under four baseline observation structures on the same joint distribution class, demonstrating the value of additional pseudo-labels. We also construct a validation-selected (VS) estimator using an independent labeled validation sample to choose the weight. The VS estimator satisfies an expected-risk oracle inequality and preserves the improvement over the baseline minimax risks with the same total labeled-data budget. Simulations and an application to predicting homeless counts illustrate the gains of the proposed estimators.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: 37 pages, 24 figures, 26 tables. Code, configurations and seeded pipelines: https://github.com/rzn-git/quantum_grid_attack_detection_benchmark (release v2.1.0)

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $π_v/β_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(π_v/β_v)r_v(y)$, where $r_v$ is agent $v$'s reward, and the rule is cardinal. If the reference is fixed and the challenger aggregated, the agents' policies at a fixed point generally differ, and any weighted mean of them is an approximate maximal lottery whatever the weights, so the dynamics select no weighting. If both are aggregated, the rule is ordinal: averaged over rounds, the collective policy is a maximal lottery of the influence-weighted preference kernel, up to a slack that we bound. Where a collective rule exists, its weights depend only on the attention weights and the temperatures.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: A theory of inductive node-level generalization from a single large graph
Statistical Machine Learning.summary:
In Graph Machine Learning (GML), the notion of generalization fundamentally varies depending on the task level and the properties of the dataset. For instance, graph-level tasks fit into the traditional ML framework of i.i.d. samples, with relatively small graphs. On the contrary, node-level tasks involve dependent nodes, often in a few large graphs. Existing studies often consider the transductive settings, where training and test data co-exist in the same graph, or, for inductive learning, try to recover some kind of probabilistic ``independence'', e.g. by still assuming a large number of independent graphs or subgraphs.
  In this work, we develop a novel framework to express the generalization capabilities of Graph ML algorithms for inductive node-level tasks when learning from a single large graph, taking inspiration from the literature on GNN transferability. In particular, we emphasize the similarities with classical ML by revisiting the excess risk decomposition with a new notion of ``transferable'' risk on large graphs. We apply this framework to Latent Position random graphs: we uncover new insights on the hardness of GML compared to traditional ML, and derive novel notions of concentration. Finally, we apply this framework to several models of GNNs, unifying several existing results on GNNs transferability and universality.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Dataset Distillation Efficiently Encodes Low-Dimensional Representations from Gradient-Based Learning of Non-Linear Tasks
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Dataset distillation, a training-aware data compression technique, has recently attracted increasing attention as an effective tool for mitigating costs of optimization and data storage. However, progress remains largely empirical. Mechanisms underlying the extraction of task-relevant information from the training process and the efficient encoding of such information into synthetic data points remain elusive. In this paper, we theoretically analyze practical algorithms of dataset distillation applied to the gradient-based training of two-layer neural networks with width $L$. By focusing on a non-linear task structure called multi-index model, we prove that the low-dimensional structure of the problem is efficiently encoded into the resulting distilled data. This dataset reproduces a model with high generalization ability for a required memory complexity of $\tildeΘ$$(r^2d+L)$, where $d$ and $r$ are the input and intrinsic dimensions of the task. To the best of our knowledge, this is one of the first theoretical works that include a specific task structure, leverage its intrinsic dimensionality to quantify the compression rate and study dataset distillation implemented solely via gradient-based algorithms.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Robbing Peter to Pay Paul: Cross-Attribute Externalities of Fairness Interventions
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Fairness interventions often targets disparities associated with a single sensitive attribute in binary classification tasks. However, when multiple sensitive attributes are associated with a data subject, improving fairness with respect to one attribute does not necessarily improve it across all attributes: it may exacerbate disparities associated with other sensitive attributes, including those that are unavailable to the practitioner. We refer to these unintended effects as cross-attribute externalities of fairness. We study how fairness with respect to one sensitive attribute varies when an initially unfair classification or regression model is corrected with respect to another attribute. We characterize these externalities using Wasserstein barycentric disparities and develop a distributional framework that captures changes in both marginal and joint fairness measures. This highlights a limitation of conventional fairness evaluation, in which the success of an intervention is assessed mainly for the attribute it targets. In a jointly Gaussian model, we derive explicit trajectories for marginal and joint disparities and identify conditions under which an intervention eliminates disparities with respect to its target attribute while increasing disparities associated with another attribute. We also derive sharp partial-identification bounds on the resulting externalities when a sensitive attribute is unavailable and extend our results to categorical sensitive attributes. We illustrate these externalities using classification and regression real-data: in the classification experiments, interventions increase unfairness with respect to the hidden attribute in the majority of scenarios across more than half of the datasets considered; in the regression experiments on the ACSIncome dataset, correcting for race reduces sex disparities, whereas subsequently correcting for age increases them.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Fast and Consistent Structure Learning in Graphical Models via Approximate Cross-Validation
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Structure learning for sparse graphical models in high dimensions requires both computational scalability and selection consistency. Classical criteria such as (Extended) Bayesian Information Criterion can provide consistency, but rely on model-specific likelihoods and complexity calibration. In comparison, cross-validation avoids such analytic calibration and is therefore attractive for graph learning. However, cross-validation is computationally infeasible and theoretically inconsistent in structure learning. This creates a tension between consistency and flexibility in modeling. In this work, we resolve the tension by developing a scalable graph-recovery procedure built on approximate cross-validation. We demonstrate its effectiveness in learning large graphical models both theoretically and empirically, and establish selection consistency under mild signal strength assumptions.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Stochastic Deep Learning: A Probabilistic Framework for Modeling Uncertainty in Structured Temporal Data
Statistical Machine Learning.summary:
I propose a novel framework that integrates stochastic differential equations (SDEs) with deep generative models to improve uncertainty quantification in machine learning applications involving structured and temporal data. This approach, termed Stochastic Latent Differential Inference (SLDI), embeds an Itô SDE in the latent space of a variational autoencoder, allowing for flexible, continuous-time modeling of uncertainty while preserving a principled mathematical foundation. The drift and diffusion terms of the SDE are parameterized by neural networks, enabling data-driven inference and generalizing classical time series models to handle irregular sampling and complex dynamic structure.
  A central theoretical contribution is the co-parameterization of the adjoint state with a dedicated neural network, forming a coupled forward-backward system that captures not only latent evolution but also gradient dynamics. I introduce a pathwise-regularized adjoint loss and analyze variance-reduced gradient flows through the lens of stochastic calculus, offering new tools for improving training stability in deep latent SDEs. My paper unifies and extends variational inference, continuous-time generative modeling, and control-theoretic optimization, providing a rigorous foundation for future developments in stochastic probabilistic machine learning.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Precise Asymptotics of Non-Convex M-Estimators
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Precise asymptotic theory for M-estimators in high-dimensional settings is largely limited to convex or mildly non-convex formulations, yet non-convex loss functions as well as regularizers are widely used in practice. We study M-estimation in generalized linear models (GLMs) where the loss function or the regularizer can be non-convex. Under rotationally invariant design matrices in the proportional asymptotic regime, we analyze the problem through Vector Approximate Message Passing (VAMP), whose iterates are described by a low-dimensional deterministic recursion called State Evolution (SE). Existing proofs of SE require the proximal operators of the loss function and the regularizer to be Lipschitz, but a non-convex loss or regularizer can have a discontinuous proximal operator, and the usual Onsager terms in VAMP then miss the contribution of the discontinuities. Assuming that the proximal operators are special functions of locally bounded variation, we derive a correction to the Onsager terms using a distributional Stein's lemma. We prove that SE holds for the corrected VAMP. We apply the theory to analyze group sparse regression with an $\ell_0$-type penalty and to robust regression with the Cauchy loss.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension $D$ exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy. After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using an exploration schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. An efficient recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bringing the overall time complexity per step to $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3+D\log D)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Well-Conditioned Oblivious Perturbations in Linear Space
Statistical Machine Learning.summary:
Perturbing a deterministic $n$-dimensional matrix with small Gaussian noise is a cornerstone of smoothed analysis of algorithms [Spielman and Teng, JACM 2004], as it reduces the condition number of the input to $O(n)$, and with it the complexity of many matrix algorithms. However, when deployed algorithmically, these perturbations are expensive due to the cost of generating and storing $n^2$ Gaussian random variables. We propose a perturbation that requires generating and storing $O(n)$ random numbers in $O(\log n)$ bits of precision, and reduces the condition number of any deterministic matrix to $O(n)$, matching Gaussian perturbations. Our result takes a step towards derandomizing matrix perturbations in numerical linear algebra, and in particular, implies that we can solve an $n\times n$ linear system to within $\varepsilon$ backward error in $O(n^2\log(n)/\varepsilon)$ time using only $O(n\log n)$ random bits.
  In our construction, we introduce the concept of a pattern matrix, which is a dense deterministic matrix that maps all sparse vectors into dense vectors in a way that goes beyond the classical uncertainty principle of the Fourier transform. We combine this with a sparse perturbation whose entries are dependent and located in a non-uniform fashion. In order to analyze this construction, we develop new techniques for lower bounding the smallest singular value of a random matrix with dependent entries.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Contextual Distributionally Robust Optimization with Causal and Continuous Structure
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: WWe propose a framework for contextual distributionally robust optimization (DRO) that considers the causal and continuous structure of the underlying distribution, and we develop interpretable and tractable decision rules. We first introduce the causal Sinkhorn discrepancy (CSD), an entropy-regularized causal Wasserstein distance that encourages continuous transport plans while preserving causal consistency. We then formulate a contextual DRO model with a CSD-based ambiguity set, termed Causal Sinkhorn DRO (Causal-SDRO), and derive its strong dual reformulation, where the worst-case distribution is characterized as a mixture of Gibbs distributions. To obtain an (infinite-dimensional) optimal policy, we propose a soft regression forest (SRF) decision rule: it preserves the interpretability of classical decision trees while being fully parametric, differentiable, and Lipschitz-smooth, enabling intrinsic interpretation from both global and local perspectives. To solve Causal-SDRO with parametric decision rules, we develop an efficient stochastic compositional gradient algorithm that converges to an $\varepsilon$-stationary point with $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ iteration complexity and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-5})$ sample complexity. Finally, numerical results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance and interpretability of our method.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: MTL-MHOL: Predicting Online Conversions under Delayed Feedback and Data Sparsity
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: This paper proposes the model-agnostic Multi-Task Learning Multi-Head Online Learning (MTL-MHOL) framework for conversion rate (CVR) prediction. Existing approaches typically address key challenges in CVR prediction, such as delayed feedback and data sparsity, in isolation or lack flexibility and practical applicability. MTL-MHOL adopts a time bucketing approach to account for delayed feedback and combines it with multi-task learning of an auxiliary task to mitigate data sparsity. We evaluate the framework on proprietary datasets from a private company and on a public dataset from Criteo. MTL-MHOL matches or outperforms all benchmark models in terms of Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) and Relative Cross Entropy (RCE), and it correctly captures temporal trends in the data using an MLP backbone, while maintaining strong performance with a DeepFM backbone. In particular, MTL-MHOL matches the performance of the advanced delayed-feedback method FSIW, outperforms the entire-space approach ESMM by 21.5% in RCE, and achieves up to 81% lift in RCE compared to the best-performing classical benchmark.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: What Environment Invariance Identifies: Minimal Invariant Sets in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Invariant causal prediction identifies the direct causes of a target $Y$ by searching for covariate sets whose conditional law of $Y$ is stable across environments. We state that criterion at the level of operators, calling a set $S$ invariant when the conditional mean embeddings of $Y$ given $X_S$ agree across environments, and characterise the resulting family exactly: under two conditions on the environments, which we state separately because they fail independently, the invariant sets are precisely those containing $PA(Y)$ and no descendant of $Y$. Two consequences follow. Invariance does not identify $PA(Y)$ uniquely, since every descendant-free superset is invariant as well; and $PA(Y)$ is the unique minimal invariant set. In finite samples, recovery requires the non-invariant sets to be separated from invariance by a margin, and the sample size splits into a screening term logarithmic in the ambient dimension and a term inherited from conditional mean embedding estimation, which is the binding one. The characterisation yields two selection rules with different failure modes, of which the conservative one controls false positives. Controlled experiments verify each population prediction directly, including the failure of uniqueness. They also show that invariance testing is a practical bottleneck: two natural designs are severely miscalibrated, while the selected test reduces but does not eliminate Type I error inflation.

Statistical Machine Learning.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference
Statistical Machine Learning.summary: Tensor network (TN) kernel machines speed up supervised learning by using low-rank TNs to reduce computation and memory. Most of these methods, however, are deterministic: they ignore parameter uncertainty, and their model complexity has to be tuned manually. Bayesian TN kernel machines remove both limitations, but only for the CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition (CPD), which has a single rank. For the more general tensor train (TT), manual tuning is even more costly, since every one of its ranks must be chosen. In this paper we propose Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines (BTT-KM), which place hierarchical ARD-type priors on the TT cores and infer all TT ranks and feature dimensions from data. Mean-field variational inference leads to a Bayesian alternating least squares algorithm with the same computational complexity as its deterministic counterpart, and gives a closed-form predictive distribution. On synthetic data, BTT-KM shrinks an over-parameterized initialization to a low-rank model close to the ground truth, and on UCI benchmarks it is competitive with state-of-the-art methods, with predictive coverage closest to the nominal value.
Statistical Machine Learning.comment: 35 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables, 1 algorithm. v2: added experiments on UCI benchmarks with a comparison to state-of-the-art methods. Code available at https://github.com/afrakilic/BTTKM

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn a strong representation of normal training data; (2) target encoder distillation aims to modulate over-generalization of I-JEPA representations to abnormal data; (3) pseudo-anomaly classification aims to calibrate anomaly predictions by learning a tight boundary around the normal data manifold. To demonstrate our design, we carry out comprehensive experiments on six datasets covering various medical image domains (e.g. MRI, OCT, X-ray, histopathology), comparing our MADJEPA with numerous state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our carefully designed world model, MADJEPA, attains competitive results, ranking first on three datasets. Our ablation studies further confirm the utility of each training stage, indicating that I-JEPA alone is not sufficient to obtain competitive results in medical anomaly detection. We publicly release our code at https://github.com/Sabina085/madjepa.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: InterGS+: Inter-Frame Gaussian Splatting Compression with Geometry-Aware Transformer Prediction and Adaptive Residual Coding
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides real-time photorealistic rendering, but representing each frame as irregular Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes creates substantial storage and transmission cost. Exploiting temporal redundancy is challenging because Gaussian primitives do not preserve fixed identities across frames. We propose InterGS+, a lightweight post-hoc inter-frame codec that jointly improves temporal prediction and residual representation. Current-frame geometry is coded with G-PCC and reconstructed before prediction, enabling consistent temporal neighborhoods at encoder and decoder. Attributes are predicted using lightweight KNN and bilateral predictors together with a geometry-aware transformer for spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance, with per-Gaussian mode selection. Residual coding is adapted to each attribute: SH innovations are coded in a shared PCA domain using vector quantization with refinement, opacity and scale in activated gamma-companded domains, and rotation as canonicalized quaternion innovations using vector quantization and refinement. On MPEG dynamic sequences, InterGS+ achieves average BD-rate reductions of 45.48% over G-PCC Amd. 1 and 7.78% over InterGS-Lite, with corresponding BD-PSNR gains of 9.98 dB and 1.10 dB. Average decoding complexity is 0.049 ms/Gaussian, demonstrating efficient streamable dynamic 3DGS compression.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the 2027 Data Compression Conference (DCC 2027)

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Super-resolved digital terrain models for GEDI geolocation correction: agreement with airborne LiDAR DTM-based corrections at the beam level, not the footprint level
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: The Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) mission measures three-dimensional forest structure with a LiDAR instrument aboard the International Space Station. GEDI observations have geolocation errors of about 10 m, which cause misalignment with other remote sensing data and reduce the accuracy of downstream tasks. Matching GEDI ground elevations against high-resolution digital terrain models (DTMs) from airborne LiDAR is one way to correct these errors, but such DTMs exist in few regions. To widen this method's applicability, we super-resolved a more widely available low-resolution DTM for elevation matching. We ask whether a super-resolved DTM yields the same correction as a 1 m-resolution airborne LiDAR DTM and, if not, why. In steep forests of western Japan, we super-resolved an existing 10 m-resolution DTM to 1 m. Additionally fusing a global 30 m-resolution DTM from a different source substantially improved the accuracy. Using the resulting DTM, we corrected GEDI observation positions first by a single offset per ground track, then point by point. For most tracks, the per-track corrections nearly agreed with those from the airborne LiDAR DTM. Point-by-point corrections, however, did not agree. This was because the error of the generated DTM was close to the elevation differences that point-by-point correction must resolve, and most of this error lay at scales that even a 10 m-resolution DTM can represent. Under similar conditions, a super-resolved DTM may be usable in place of a 1 m-resolution DTM for per-track correction, but improving the accuracy, or using it for point-by-point correction as well, requires reducing the error at these scales rather than reproducing fine relief.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 34 pages, 12 figures, 18 tables

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Complete virtual unwrapping and reading of a rolled Herculaneum papyrus
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: The carbonized papyrus scrolls from Herculaneum preserve the only large-scale library to survive from classical antiquity. Many scrolls have remained unread because physical unrolling risks irreversible damage. Non-invasive imaging offers a route to their texts, yet previous work on sealed Herculaneum scrolls has recovered only localized readings. Here, by combining high-resolution X-ray computed microtomography ($μ$CT) data acquired on the BM18 beamline at the ESRF with machine-learning-assisted virtual unwrapping, we study three still-closed scrolls. For PHerc. 1667, a remnant of earlier attempts at physical unrolling, we achieve the complete unwrapping and reading of the preserved writing surface, making it the first Herculaneum papyrus read completely by virtual unwrapping. The text was transcribed and cross-verified by nine papyrologists. In PHerc.
