Paris. 4, the source of the Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize text, the high-resolution scan makes ink directly visible in the tomographic volume, allowing 3D ink segmentation and comparison of recovered text with visible deposits. In PHerc. 139, we recover title and author-attribution evidence identifying the scroll as Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8. These results establish a basis for the ongoing, systematic recovery and scholarly study of texts preserved within the still-closed Herculaneum library.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Preprint, 54 pages including Extended Data and Supplementary Information, 6 main figures. Added workflow and surface-rendering figures and revised the abstract, methods, and papyrological transcription

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Flux Compensation as a Prerequisite for Temporal CT: Per-Bundle Cramér-Rao Floors and Estimators That Reach Them
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: In Temporal CT (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work measured the resulting per-bundle cost as a Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), using one incident count $N_0$ for all rays and a learned prior trained on one patient; this paper removes both restrictions. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, approximately equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a bias-corrected, box-projected Gauss-Newton Poisson likelihood iteration. V8c, a neural network trained on 19 patients, corrects SNN2. T2bp, an empirical-Bayes post-processor without trained weights, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior from the patient's own bundles. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramér-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of the baseline's incident photons, near the equal-attenuation 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below GE-type bow-ties. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median MSE ratio 1.02); holding air paths at zero, a box-constrained maximum likelihood estimate lowers the ratio to 0.88, and T2bp$\circ$SNN2 to 0.89 (0.74-1.26); T2bp's per-patient prior adds measurably only in the deeper bins (a median 12-29% over all bins). T2bp$\circ$SNN2 beats T2bp$\circ$V8c on three of four N$_0$FC test cells, but trails or ties it on the four N$_0$FC validation volumes. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired outside its corpus's exposure rule. Flux compensation, chiefly the bow-tie, is a prerequisite; classical estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining 3- to 6-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: v3: condensed and retitled (v2: "Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Training-Free Empirical-Bayes Estimation"); adds a box-constrained ML estimate, bootstrap test-cell verdicts and a table of development choices made with test-patient data. 77 pages (26 main, 51 supplementary), 8 figures, 25 tables. Companion to arXiv:2604.10934

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Exact Volume-Preserving Diffeomorphic Shear Splitting: Continuous-Discrete Geometric Bounds, Reversible Memory Backpropagation, and Expressivity Frontiers in Volumetric Mapping
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary:
Incompressible diffeomorphic registration requires continuous spatial mappings that preserve local tissue volume (det(DΦ) = 1) without topological folding (det(DΦ) > 0). Standard velocity-field methods (SVF, LDDMM) approximate incompressibility via numerical ODE integration or soft penalties, exhibiting numerical volume drift (~10^-4 to 10^-1), iterative grid inversions, and linear backpropagation memory O(L * N_vox).
  We formulate an exact structure-preserving framework for 3D registration based on cascaded coordinate shears. By decomposing the divergence-free Lie algebra sdiff(Ω) into six coordinate-shear generators whose convective non-linearities vanish identically, each elementary stage integrates analytically to a closed-form triangular shear with det(DS_k) = 1 and exact machine-precision inverse requiring zero iterations and zero spatial interpolations. Multi-stage compositions generate the connected volume-preserving group SDiff_0(Ω). We establish: (i) an unconditional global diffeomorphism proof closing the Hadamard-Caccioppoli injectivity gap; (ii) a Dirichlet boundary confinement lemma; (iii) an anisotropic Riemannian similarity invariance; (iv) a Sobolev H^2 spectral budget preventing chaotic mixing; and (v) an exact reversible backpropagation engine eliminating O(L) trajectory storage (0.00 MB intermediate activations).
  We prove second-order O(h^2) sub-voxel convergence across 16^3 to 64^3 lattices and second-order trajectory accuracy for palindromic Strang splitting (468.1x error reduction vs. Lie-Trotter; drift |det(DΦ)-1| <= 2.22e-16). Execution is 2.1x-4.0x faster than SVF with 78.4% GPU memory reduction. On cardiac cine-MRI (ACDC, N=100) and brain MRI (OASIS-1, N=414), our model achieves competitive Dice (0.884 and 0.841) while strictly maintaining 0.0000% folding and zero volume drift.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 17 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Reversible PyTorch autograd engine with exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism guarantees

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Demographic Encoding is Not Exposure: Fairness and Privacy in Chest X-ray Foundation Models
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Medical foundation models encode patient demographics and can reveal whether a patient was in the training set, and these properties are often treated as one problem. We tested whether they are aligned by measuring demographic encoding, diagnostic fairness gaps and membership-inference vulnerability on the same models. We trained 200 linear or multilayer-perceptron (MLP) heads on frozen BiomedCLIP, DINOv2 and RAD-DINO embeddings, with three seeds, and audited them on CheXpert and NIH ChestX-ray14. Demographic encoding explained almost no variance in patient vulnerability, and all 72 CheXpert associations were statistically equivalent to zero. Erasing linearly decodable demographics left leakage unchanged but reduced age-related underdiagnosis gaps. Leakage depended instead on head capacity and training length. On RAD-DINO, a linear head reached a membership-inference area under the curve (AUC) of 0.694, compared with 0.907 for a 30-epoch MLP, at similar test performance. Fairness and privacy should therefore be audited separately, and linear heads or shorter training reduce leakage with little or no loss of utility. The code is available on GitHub for public use.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Enhancing Diabetic Retinopathy Detection with CNN-Based Models: A Comparative Study of UNET and Stacked UNET Architectures
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Diabetic Retinopathy DR is a severe complication of diabetes. Damaged or abnormal blood vessels can cause loss of vision. The need for massive screening of a large population of diabetic patients has generated an interest in a computer-aided fully automatic diagnosis of DR. In the realm of Deep learning frameworks, particularly convolutional neural networks CNNs, have shown great interest and promise in detecting DR by analyzing retinal images. However, several challenges have been faced in the application of deep learning in this domain. High-quality, annotated datasets are scarce, and the variations in image quality and class imbalances pose significant hurdles in developing a dependable model. In this paper, we demonstrate the proficiency of two Convolutional Neural Networks CNNs based models, UNET and Stacked UNET utilizing the APTOS Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society Dataset. This system achieves an accuracy of 92.81% for the UNET and 93.32% for the stacked UNET architecture. The architecture classifies the images into five categories ranging from 0 to 4, where 0 is no DR and 4 is proliferative DR.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Geospatial foundation models and deep learning for climate resilience: a review of transfer, uncertainty and decision readiness
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Geospatial foundation models can reuse information learned from large Earth-observation archives, but their value for climate resilience depends on whether that information transfers to unfamiliar events, regions and observing conditions. This review connects advances in deep learning with the evidence needed for hazard monitoring and early warning. A descriptive audit of 137 full-text hazard-application studies is interpreted alongside a separate corpus of 37 model and benchmark records. Ninety-eight application studies reported an out-of-distribution experiment, whereas headline evaluations included held-out events in 31 studies, regions in 25 and sensors in only two. None of the ten studies coded for geospatial foundation-model fine-tuning used sensor holdout as a headline test. Uncertainty-related methods were recorded in 16 studies, including two with explicitly calibrated probabilistic output. These overlapping counts describe evaluation practice within the coded corpus, not a ranking of model families. We distinguish Earth-observation representation learning from atmospheric forecasting and examine how labels, observability, forecast lead time and decision requirements constrain their contribution across flood, wildfire, drought, heat, cryosphere and cascading-hazard applications. We then develop a decision-backward evaluation framework: define the action and information available when it must be taken, reproduce the relevant shift, retain a matched task-specific baseline, and report misses, false alarms, reliability and end-to-end latency. The framework turns transferability from a broad model claim into a testable requirement for climate adaptation and risk management.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Preprint submitted to Frontiers in Climate

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Model-Assisted Probability of Detection Studies for Image-Based Human Inspection
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Establishing a probability of detection (POD) curve is important for assessing the reliability of components in aging systems. Traditional POD studies rely on physical specimens containing representative flaws and human inspectors who record detection results, making such studies costly. This paper demonstrates how appropriately validated physics-based simulation can substantially reduce, and in suitable applications potentially replace, physical POD experiments. We use XRSIM, an X-ray radiographic simulator, to generate weld images containing cracks of varying size, morphology, and location. Flaw characteristics, locations, and the number of flaws per image were randomized, with images containing zero to three flaws. Each simulated flaw is treated as an observational unit contributing flaw-level hit-miss responses. To capture human inspection variability, the images were presented in random order to five inspectors, each of whom inspected the images twice. The resulting data were analyzed using a repeated-measures binary-regression model accounting for flaw-to-flaw, inspector-to-inspector, flaw/inspector-combination, and inspection-to-inspection variability. Bayesian inference was used to estimate the population-mean POD curve, inspector-specific POD curves, and associated statistical uncertainty. Results show that flaw-to-flaw variability dominates, with appreciable differences among inspectors. The study provides a framework for combining physics-based image simulation with controlled human inspection to estimate POD while reducing the experimental burden of physical specimen fabrication.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 31 pages, 15 figures, 2 tables

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Training-Free Continuous Bitrate Control for Scalable Image Coding for Humans and Machines
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Continuous variable-rate compression is highly demanded in real-world applications, but remains underexplored in scalable image coding for humans and machines. In this paper, we propose a training-free variable-rate scalable image coding framework. By adaptively adjusting quantization step sizes based on predicted scale values, the proposed method enables independent and continuous bitrate control for the machine and enhancement layers while preserving important latent information in each layer. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and highlight the importance of bitrate allocation between the two layers.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted to IEEE 15th Global Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE GCCE 2026)

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Generalizable Variable-Rate Adaptation for Image Coding for Machines
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Image Coding for Machines (ICM) aims to preserve task-relevant information for machine vision under limited bitrates. However, most ICM models are trained for a fixed operating point, and extending them to variable-rate compression is challenging because their training objectives differ across tasks and model designs. In this paper, we propose a loss-agnostic distillation framework for variable-rate ICM. A pretrained fixed-rate ICM model is used as a frozen teacher, while a student model learns variable-rate behavior through importance-adaptive quantization and distillation-based optimization. This enables continuous bitrate control with a single model while preserving task-relevant latent components, without requiring the original task-specific loss or downstream task labels. Experiments based on existing ICM models demonstrate that the proposed method provides continuous bitrate control and achieves competitive recognition performance compared with the fixed-rate models.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted to 2026 IEEE International Conference on Visual Communications and Image Processing (IEEE VCIP 2026)

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: PoRef-MIL: Plug-and-Play Posterior Refinement for Multiple Instance Learning in QSM-Based Brain Disease Classification
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) is a novel quantitative MRI contrast for studying tissue susceptibility changes in brain disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple sclerosis (MS). However, small cohorts and the lack of local annotations make developing deep learning models for QSM-based diagnosis challenging. In this work, we propose PoRef-MIL, a weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework combining iterative slice relabeling and network retraining with a plug-and-play posterior refinement module (PRM). During training, a 2D dual-branch diagnosis network and a subject-level classifier were alternately trained for five rounds. The classifier was used to update slice pseudo-labels for retraining the diagnosis network. The PRM was applied during inference to refine slice probabilities through bidirectional posterior inference and calculate entropy-derived confidence from the refined probabilities, which was then used in sliding-window scoring to obtain subject-level predictions. PoRef-MIL was evaluated on an in-house PD cohort of 287 participants and a public MS cohort of 150 participants. Compared with eight classification methods, PoRef-MIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.942 and 0.872, and accuracies of 0.926 and 0.833, for PD and MS classification, respectively. Ablation experiments were conducted to validate the effectiveness of iterative relabeling and PRM, and the plug-and-play feature of the proposed PRM was also evaluated using four state-of-the-art MIL models. Overall, PoRef-MIL offers a promising approach to QSM-based disease classification in small cohorts without manual slice annotations.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 5figure, 6tables;

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: orGAN: A Synthetic Data Augmentation Pipeline for Simultaneous Generation of Surgical Images and Ground Truth Labels
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep learning for surgical image analysis is constrained by limited data diversity, ethical restrictions, high acquisition costs, and the scarcity of accurately annotated bleeding datasets, making reliable bleeding localization particularly challenging. To address these limitations, we propose orGAN, a modular framework that generates realistic, fully annotated synthetic surgical bleeding images together with recoverable point-level supervision. To overcome the ethical and cost barriers of real surgical data, the pipeline is trained on silicone-based mimicking organs that reproduce tissue properties, using an enhanced StyleGAN3 generator coupled with Relational Positional Learning to embed bleeding coordinates, a Surgical Label Detection Algorithm to recover coordinate and mask labels, and a fine-tuned LaMa inpainting network to restore clean image-label pairs. To compensate for scarce annotations, Bleeding Alert Map (BAM) localization models are trained on a blend of synthetic and mimicking-organ images. The enhanced StyleGAN3 attains an Inception Score of 2.24, and the inpainting network preserves realism at a mean SSIM of 0.98. The blended model outperforms both single-source baselines, reaching a Dice coefficient of 0.635 on paired bleeding frames. With a stronger Pix2PixHD backbone, Dice rises to 0.893 with a centroid error of 6.3 pixels. On real Hamlyn surgical video, the blended model achieves a frame-level accuracy of 0.858 and a bleeding-frame detection rate of 0.998 on Hamlyn 2, where all 500 frames were annotated as bleeding-positive. These results show that combining realistic synthetic images with mimicking-organ data is an effective, ethical, and economical strategy for developing surgical AI under limited annotated data.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 39 pages, 10figures

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Where does pancreatic lesion segmentation fail on public CT? An attenuation-stratified analysis of a duct-guided pipeline on PanTS
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Lesion segmentation is a building block of most CT pipelines for pancreatic cancer detection, yet lesion overlap scores stay low. Instead of proposing a new architecture, we report where an end-to-end pipeline fails on a large public dataset. On PanTS we built a three-stage pipeline: pancreas segmentation, maps of the main pancreatic duct (MPD) and common bile duct (CBD), and a lesion model that receives the CT with or without the predicted duct maps. Both lesion models were trained identically on 4007 scans and evaluated once on 737 held-out test scans (127 with a lesion) under a comparison rule fixed before the test run. Lesion Dice was 0.213 with duct maps and 0.209 with CT only (paired difference +0.004, 95% CI -0.011 to +0.019). The duct maps raised the share of lesions touched by a prediction (+0.079, 95% CI +0.024 to +0.134) but also enlarged predictions in lesion-free scans, and lesion-like regions were predicted in all lesion-free test scans. Out of fold, keeping only the predicted components that touched the lesion raised Dice only from 0.285 to 0.309; the loss came mainly from the extent of correctly located predictions. Clearly hypoattenuating lesions, which intensity alone separates from normal pancreas, had the lowest coverage (median 16.6%). From the predicted maps alone, the MPD diameter separated lesion from lesion-free test scans with AUC 0.794 (95% CI 0.747 to 0.839), while the CBD diameter was weak (AUC 0.603) and added nothing. Code for training, inference and evaluation is publicly available.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/Kang812/pants-lesion-failure-analysis

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: MusicRec: Audio, Lyrics, and Engagement Feature Enrichment for Music Recommendation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Music recommendation systems typically treat songs as opaque tokens, relying on interaction histories that overlook semantic or acoustic content. Prior LLM-augmented, multimodal, and text-enhanced sequential recommenders partially combine semantic, acoustic, or engagement signals, and none jointly model all three within a unified LLM-based framework grounded in song content. In this work, we propose a multimodal framework for session-based music recommendation that enriches the LastFM-1K dataset with three complementary signals: (1) audio and lyric embeddings from pretrained music and text models, (2) LLM-generated semantic metadata using the MGPHot schema, and (3) listening completion ratios. We validate the generated metadata against human MGPHot annotations across all 58 attributes. We extend the E4SRec framework with multimodal features, ItemID encoder backbones including SASRec, BERT4Rec, and GRU4Rec, and LLM backbones including LLaMA-2-13B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and LLaMA-3-70B across zero-shot and fine-tuned settings. In addition, we evaluate four multimodal fusion strategies, benchmark five audio and five lyric encoders, and compare Spotify audio attributes with LLM-generated MGPHot metadata. Our experiments show that content-based features improve over ID-only baselines by up to 95% in Recall and 79% in NDCG, with the largest gains when the ItemID baseline is weakest. Fine-tuning substantially improves over zero-shot, after which the best audio or lyric setup outperforms the ID-only baseline for every backbone. Naive multimodal fusion does not always yield additive improvements, highlighting challenges in cross-modal integration, while structured LLM-generated metadata proves more useful than Spotify audio attributes. We release a large-scale multimodal benchmark for music recommendation research.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted at IEEE BigData 2026. Extended version: 18 pages, 5 figures, 14 tables

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: SpA2V: Harnessing Spatial Auditory Cues for Audio-driven Spatially-aware Video Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Audio-driven video generation aims to synthesize realistic videos that align with input audio recordings, akin to the human ability to visualize scenes from auditory input. However, existing approaches predominantly focus on exploring semantic information, such as the classes of sounding sources present in the audio, limiting their ability to generate videos with accurate content and spatial composition. In contrast, we humans can not only naturally identify the semantic categories of sounding sources but also determine their deeply encoded spatial attributes, including locations and movement directions. This useful information can be elucidated by considering specific spatial indicators derived from the inherent physical properties of sound, such as loudness or frequency. As prior methods largely ignore this factor, we present SpA2V, the first framework explicitly exploits these spatial auditory cues from audios to generate videos with high semantic and spatial correspondence. SpA2V decomposes the generation process into two stages: 1) Audio-guided Video Planning: We meticulously adapt a state-of-the-art MLLM for a novel task of harnessing spatial and semantic cues from input audio to construct Video Scene Layouts (VSLs). This serves as an intermediate representation to bridge the gap between the audio and video modalities. 2) Layout-grounded Video Generation: We develop an efficient and effective approach to seamlessly integrate VSLs as conditional guidance into pre-trained diffusion models, enabling VSL-grounded video generation in a training-free manner. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpA2V excels in generating realistic videos with semantic and spatial alignment to the input audios.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: The 33rd ACM Multimedia Conference (MM '25) | Page: https://spa2v.tkpham.me

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: TALE: Training-free Cross-domain Image Composition via Adaptive Latent Manipulation and Energy-guided Optimization
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: We present TALE, a novel training-free framework harnessing the generative capabilities of text-to-image diffusion models to address the cross-domain image composition task that focuses on flawlessly incorporating user-specified objects into a designated visual contexts regardless of domain disparity. Previous methods often involve either training auxiliary networks or finetuning diffusion models on customized datasets, which are expensive and may undermine the robust textual and visual priors of pre-trained diffusion models. Some recent works attempt to break the barrier by proposing training-free workarounds that rely on manipulating attention maps to tame the denoising process implicitly. However, composing via attention maps does not necessarily yield desired compositional outcomes. These approaches could only retain some semantic information and usually fall short in preserving identity characteristics of input objects or exhibit limited background-object style adaptation in generated images. In contrast, TALE is a novel method that operates directly on latent space to provide explicit and effective guidance for the composition process to resolve these problems. Specifically, we equip TALE with two mechanisms dubbed Adaptive Latent Manipulation and Energy-guided Latent Optimization. The former formulates noisy latents conducive to initiating and steering the composition process by directly leveraging background and foreground latents at corresponding timesteps, and the latter exploits designated energy functions to further optimize intermediate latents conforming to specific conditions that complement the former to generate desired final results. Our experiments demonstrate that TALE surpasses prior baselines and attains state-of-the-art performance in image-guided composition across various photorealistic and artistic domains.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: The 32nd ACM Multimedia Conference (MM '24) | Code: https://github.com/ptkvn/tale | Page: https://tale.tkpham.me

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: ASSEMBLE: Atomic Skills for Evidence-Grounded Video Reasoning
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Complex video reasoning often depends on evidence scattered across distant moments, entities, and events, yet a correct answer alone does not reveal whether a model relied on the right parts of the video. We introduce ASSEMBLE, a framework that makes supporting evidence explicit throughout long-video reasoning. It organizes local observations and cross-clip narratives into timestamped evidence catalogs traceable to the source video. A grounding-aware reader then composes question-specific atomic skills whose structured outputs include explicit evidence references and support assessments. Following teacher-supervised fine-tuning, we train the reader with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) using answer correctness and correctness-gated citation alignment. The resulting reasoning traces are inspectable, and final predictions remain linked to explicit supporting evidence. With a 9B reader supervised by a 235B teacher and shared precomputed evidence catalogs, ASSEMBLE achieves 59.2% macro-averaged answer accuracy across three long-video reasoning benchmarks, compared with 58.3% for Gemini-2.5-Pro, while improving macro-averaged overlap-based Grounded accuracy by 6.7 percentage points, with gains on all three benchmarks. Ablations show that, under the same post-trained reader and inference budget, structured skill inference improves overlap-based Grounded accuracy over free-form reasoning. Compared with generic structured reasoning, the benefit is more setting-dependent, with the clearest answer-accuracy gain on VRBench. These results show that explicit evidence grounding can improve long-video reasoning while keeping predictions tied to their supporting evidence.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: FGAS: Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: The rapid development of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) has made high-fidelity generated audio widely available across the Internet, driving the advancement of audio steganography. Benefiting from advances in deep learning, current audio steganography schemes are mainly based on encoder-decoder network architectures. While these methods achieve promising perceptual quality, they typically require network pre-training, and maintaining anti-steganalysis performance at high payloads remains challenging. To address these issues, we propose Fixed Decoder Network-Based Audio Steganography with Adversarial Perturbation Generation (FGAS). Adversarial perturbations carrying a secret message are embedded into the cover audio to generate stego audio. The sender and receiver independently construct the same fixed decoder from a shared architecture and initialization key, avoiding the transfer of trained decoder parameters. In FGAS, we propose an Audio Adversarial Perturbation Generation (A2PG) strategy with an optional robust extension and design a lightweight fixed decoder. The fixed decoder guarantees reliable extraction of the hidden message, while adversarial perturbations are optimized to keep the stego audio perceptually and statistically close to the cover audio, thereby improving anti-steganalysis performance. The experimental results show that FGAS significantly improves stego audio quality, achieving an average PSNR gain of over 10 dB compared to SOTA methods. Furthermore, FGAS demonstrates strong robustness against common audio processing attacks. Moreover, FGAS exhibits superior anti-steganalysis performance across different relative payloads; under high-capacity embedding, it achieves a classification error rate about 2% higher, indicating stronger anti-steganalysis performance than current SOTA methods.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Straight to the Product: What Online Retailers Miss When Shoppers Ask AI First
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary:
When people ask an AI assistant what to buy, what happens next at the store? We link the same people's assistant conversations to their later browsing at twenty large online retailers. People go to the product the assistant named: among shoppers who had not visited the store in the past week, visits to the named product within a day rise from 0.02 to 2.07 per 100 answers (+2.0 points [1.7, 2.4]), and on days with a product-page visit at the store, 44% show a product from their own answer, against 1.5% for a matched answer given to someone else. The result replicates in a separate five-month period. Few arrive through the assistant's link: after recommending answers, 89% of visits carry no sign of it, and 54% follow a web search, the same share as their usual visits. When a search comes just before the first visit, it names the answer's product 28% of the time (1% in earlier weeks), as if the search box were an address bar. The chat names the product; the store logs a search. Once there, shoppers keep browsing.
  We propose product follow-through, the share of answers followed by a visit to the product they named, as a way to evaluate shopping assistants and agents by what people do next: it needs no referral data or provider logs and can be computed for each assistant.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: MusicRec: Audio, Lyrics, and Engagement Feature Enrichment for Music Recommendation

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Where Do Fact-Checking Errors Arise? Separating Retrieval, Search Control and Judgement in Evidence-Grounded Verification
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: An evidence-grounded fact-checker can fail because it does not find the evidence or because it does not use it; end-to-end accuracy does not tell the two apart. We present a protocol that follows the reference evidence from the store to the verdict and separates retrieval, search control, judgement and verdict validation. We assess 293 claims from FEVER, FEVER 2.0 and AVeriTeC with one open-weights 9B model under two evidence conditions: small stores of annotated evidence, where discovery is easy, and the full source collections. In the control condition a single hybrid retrieval pass delivers complete reference evidence for 226 of 228 evidence-bearing claims, and adaptive controllers and a tool agent spend two to nine times as many model calls without a consistent gain. Of 34 decisive claims labelled as lacking evidence, 33 have the complete evidence in the packet: in 15 the judge abstains, and in 18 validation rules overturn a decisive verdict. On AVeriTeC these rules lower single-pass accuracy by six points, to 65.0% (balanced accuracy 57.6%). Ten judges from eight model families also show abstentions and validation conversions on fixed packets. Against the full stores hybrid single-pass accuracy falls by 17 to 29 points. Wikipedia evidence recovery declines; AVeriTeC recovery changes from annotated answers to cited pages and is measured separately. No controller recovers the accuracy loss. The agent also shows no resolved gain on 714 further Wikipedia claims. Evidence recovery, judgement and validation should be measured separately before an error is attributed to search.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Multi Interests for Joint Search-Recommendation Modeling
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Search and recommendation are crucial for understanding user preferences. More and more studies are attempting to jointly model search behavior and recommendation behavior, by integrating user active search and passive recommendation behavior data to better mine user preferences. However, although existing cross-domain unified modeling frameworks can effectively compensate for the differences in behavior between domains, they overlook the expression of interests in different scenarios under mixed sequences. In this study, we propose a multi-interest-based mixed sequential modeling framework MIJSR, which performs multi-interest mining and adaptive integration on search recommendation mixed sequences from both structural and semantic perspectives. Specifically, our model can be roughly divided into three modules: cross-domain behavior fusion, multi-interest mining, and multi-task prediction. Firstly, we align the representations of query and item through contrastive learning training. Then, we extract the multi interests of the mixed behavior sequence from both structural and semantic perspectives. Structurally, we extract search interests, recommendation interests, and cross interests through subsequence partitioning and mask settings; In terms of semantics, we use the semantic information of queries for clustering and perform semantic segmentation on mixed sequences to construct semantic multi interests. Finally, the adaptive fusion of multiple interests is combined with other side information to use a progressive layered extraction model for multi-task prediction. Extensive experiments on two open-source datasets have shown that our model can further enhance its accuracy in search and recommendation by extracting users' multi interests at a fine-grained level. Codes are available at https://github.com/pxcstart/MIJSR.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: MUSES: Retrieving the Literature That Shapes a Researcher's Next Paper
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Some of the work that shapes a researcher's next paper is not something they went looking for: it may arrive before the project has a question anyone could search for. How much can be anticipated from past publications alone? We introduce MUSES, a benchmark of 1.04 million cases built from the Semantic Scholar Open Research Corpus (S2ORC), with 140,278 held-out test cases. Given a researcher's papers before a cutoff, a system ranks 2.33 million earlier candidates for their next paper, scored primarily on works they had not cited before. Because citations alone do not show what shaped a paper, we also asked authors which works shaped or inspired their papers, yielding 1,633 evaluable cases, a distinct construct from citation-based targets. A classifier grounded in human coding adds citation contexts where the next paper describes building on a work. Across lexical, dense and citation-graph retrievers and supervised models, past publications provide a useful guide to the next paper's literature, but retrieval is harder for previously uncited works. In the main comparison, history-based retrievers place a newly cited work in their top 100 for 30--37% of cases, versus 5% for popularity. Among author-collected cases, one retriever finds an author-named work in 52% of cases (30% when targets exclude previously cited works). The researcher's own history also outperforms histories from topically similar researchers. For previously uncited works, even pooling the evaluated rankings leaves 36--58% of cases without a target in any top-100 list, across citation-based and author-reported targets. Project information helps narrow this gap: in hindsight, adding the next paper's title improves retrieval, and adding its abstract improves it further. MUSES provides a benchmark for developing systems that help researchers discover literature relevant to their next project.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Web-scale recommender models evolve primarily through retraining or fine-tuning. We propose \emph{weight coding}, a methodology for model evolution through direct, executable weight edits. A large language model (LLM) agent inspects model structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and implements edits using evaluation feedback. The loop progresses from localized changes to targeted searches and composition, allowing edited components to adapt to one another. A cached engine enables rapid forward evaluation without backpropagation. On Pinterest's 147M-parameter Image Search two-tower retriever, weight coding improves held-out recall@10 of production model by up to 15.0 percentage points (+24\% relative) with few edits in about 1/4 GPU hours of a full post-training finetune, while a common launch only improves around 1\%. After reinitializing the entire 13.6M-parameter interaction module randomly while retaining the surrounding trained model, searching 2,448 mixing and normalization parameters yields 9.8 points above production. Offline gains span the full funnel including dense retrieval, generative retrieval and ranking, with up to 1.37B learnable parameters and different edits for each architecture. Steering edits provide explicit control of model performance over segments like freshness and product. Weight coding requires no serving change and online A/B tests increase saves per user from the edited retrieval source by 8.4\% to 10.7\%, aligned with the target business objectives. Our results establish weight coding as a practical and useful tool for model development and and behavioral control in a real web-scale production system, with potential to extend to both pre-training and post-training stages across the funnel.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Invisible to humans, visible to machines: a preregistered audit of Unicode fidelity across four biomedical bibliographic APIs
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: To develop a reusable, preregistered method for auditing the character-level fidelity of bibliographic application programming interfaces (APIs), and to apply it to four public APIs used to build biomedical text corpora. Preregistered audit (OSF osf.io/zjevr). From the 2024 PubMed Central (PMC) Open Access subset, a simple random sample of 4,000 English-language research articles was drawn. Abstracts returned by the PubMed E-utilities, Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were compared with the PMC Journal Article Tag Suite (JATS) XML abstract for 51 registered code points, 34 of them in four primary classes: typographic punctuation, mathematical/scientific symbols, Greek letters and special whitespace. A cell (API x class) was classified as systematic loss when the upper 95% Wilson bound of conditional preservation was below 5%, and as faithful when the lower bound exceeded 90%. The mechanism of each loss was examined in the aligned text and the raw API responses. Two of 16 cells met the loss criterion. PubMed preserved typographic punctuation in 0.6% of eligible abstracts (12/2,113; 95% CI 0.3-1.0%), replacing it with ASCII equivalents. OpenAlex preserved special whitespace in 0.0% (0/1,085; 95% CI 0.0-0.4%), which its inverted-index format cannot store. Mathematical symbols and Greek letters were preserved by all four APIs (95.2-99.7%). Crossref returned an abstract for 75.4% of papers (95% CI 74.1-76.7%) and for none published by Elsevier (0/360) or the American Chemical Society (0/105). The same published abstract reaches text-mining pipelines with different characters depending on the API that serves it. Studies that analyze characters, including character-level markers of writing assisted by large language models, should take text from a source shown to preserve those characters, or normalize all sources identically, and report the API and retrieval date.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: 22 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables, supplementary material. v2: corrected preregistration link (https://osf.io/zjevr), corrected and updated references, complete reporting of registered analyses (Supplementary Table S4), method overview (Section 3.1), revised description of the mechanism audit. Data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.20556349; code: https://github.com/P-Czum/pmc-unicode-audit

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Sequential recommender systems aim to predict a user's next interaction by modeling temporal dependencies in historical behavior sequences. To capture such dependencies, recent approaches increasingly rely on attention-based architectures, particularly transformers. While effective at modeling long-range sequential patterns, these models apply a fixed computation depth to all interaction items, treating them as equally complex. However, user behavior is inherently heterogeneous, with many interactions following simple repetitive patterns, whereas others require modeling higher-order dependencies. This mismatch leads to inefficient utilization of model capacity and unnecessary computational overhead, particularly in deep transformer-based architectures. To address this issue, we propose MoR4Rec, a sequential recommendation framework based on a Mixture-of-Recursion paradigm, which enables item-wise adaptive computation through a shared transformer backbone. A learned routing mechanism dynamically assigns each item to an appropriate recursion depth, allocating deeper computation to complex interactions while processing simpler patterns more efficiently. To improve computational efficiency, we develop a cascade-based strategy with key-value sharing across recursion steps. We further introduce a gated attention mechanism that adaptively regulates contextual information during recursive sequence modeling. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that MoR4Rec consistently outperforms strong transformer-based baselines, achieving average gains of 2.28% in Recall@5, 2.50% in NDCG@5, and 2.0% in MRR@5 over the strongest baseline. The improvements remain consistent across top-10 and top-20 recommendation cutoffs, while comparisons with vanilla transformers demonstrate the computational efficiency of adaptive recursive processing.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: VistaTree: Question Answering over Long Multimodal Documents with Image-Derived Summary Trees
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Answering questions over long multimodal documents requires locating relevant evidence across pages containing text, tables, and figures. When the document exceeds the model's context window, selective retrieval becomes necessary. We introduce VistaTree, a document question-answering agent that builds a summary tree directly from rendered page images. VistaTree segments documents into contiguous page spans, recursively groups them into a topic hierarchy, and refines sibling summaries to distinguish neighboring sections. At query time, the agent uses node summaries to select relevant nodes and reads the corresponding pages, using hierarchical navigation when the full outline exceeds the context budget. Experiments on MMLongBench-Doc and LongDocURL evaluate answer quality and retrieval cost using a locally hosted vision-language model, and quantify the performance gap between global and hierarchical access to the index.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Evaluating Small Open LLMs for Medical Question Answering: A Practical Framework
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Incorporating large language models (LLMs) in medical question answering demands more than high average accuracy: a model that returns substantively different answers each time it is queried is not a reliable medical tool. Online health communities such as Reddit have become a primary source of medical information for millions of users, yet they remain highly susceptible to misinformation; deploying LLMs as assistants in these settings amplifies the need for output consistency alongside correctness. We present a practical, open-source evaluation framework for assessing small, locally-deployable open-weight LLMs on medical question answering, treating reproducibility as a first-class metric alongside lexical and semantic accuracy. Our pipeline computes eight quality metrics, including BERTScore, ROUGE-L, and an LLM-as-judge rubric, together with two within-model reproducibility metrics derived from repeated inference (N=10 runs per question). Evaluating three models (Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 3 12B, MedGemma 1.5 4B) on 50 MedQuAD questions (N=1,500 total responses) reveals that despite low-temperature generation (T=0.2), self-agreement across runs reaches at most 0.20, while 87-97% of all outputs per model are unique -- a safety gap that single-pass benchmarks entirely miss. The clinically fine-tuned MedGemma 1.5 4B underperforms the larger general-purpose models on both quality and reproducibility; however, because MedGemma is also the smallest model, this comparison confounds domain fine-tuning with model scale. We describe the methodology in sufficient detail for practitioners to replicate or extend the evaluation for their own model-selection workflows. All code and data pipelines are available at https://github.com/aviad-buskila/llm_medical_reproducibility.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: LLM-Based Assistant for Dog Care Guidance
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: This study investigates whether domain grounding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can enhance the accuracy and reliability of pet care advice generated by large language models (LLMs). We curated a dataset of breed-specific dog care information and used it to develop two systems: a RAG pipeline based on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, and a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B model adapted using LoRA. Both systems were evaluated on 15 dog care questions. The RAG model achieved a perfect average score of 2.0, outperforming the fine-tuned model (mean = 1.47). Statistical analyses, including Welch's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (all p < 0.05), confirmed the significance of the performance gap. Our findings suggest that retrieval-based domain grounding leads to more accurate, consistent, and trustworthy responses than standalone fine-tuning in specialized LLM applications.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Bayesian Rational Search Engine User
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: A user faces a list ordered by a noisy proxy for relevance and decides whether to pay to inspect another item or stop with the best she has found. Because she does not know the page's quality, each inspection both produces a candidate and updates her beliefs about the remaining items. We show that the optimal policy is a standout rule: the user stops when her best find is sufficiently good relative to what she expects from the page, with the required margin changing with depth. The browsing dynamics collapse to a one-dimensional Markov chain, yielding the full distribution of inspection depth through a closed-form recursion. The model uncovers three reasons for stopping: trust, commit, and cut-losses, and yields testable implications. It also turns inspection depth into a learning-to-rank likelihood. Observed depth restricts the latent relevance path to a polyhedron of survival inequalities, while conversion identifies the terminal winner. Simulations show that the estimator recovers relevance under correct specification and improves ranking using only the incumbent ranker's features. Applied to public Baidu search logs, the inspection depth likelihood produces rankings that align more closely with expert relevance judgments than click-trained alternatives.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: With the growing demand for large language model (LLM) services, optimizing LLM serving systems is becoming increasingly complex, and the bottleneck is no longer predicting how a given configuration will perform. The harder problem is deciding what to investigate: which mechanisms matter for a workload, which configurations are worth testing, and what evidence a decision still needs. In this work, we present NoeVera, an agentic Second Brain that goes beyond just one-shot retrieval by turning papers, code, benchmarks, and experimental results into a persistent, provenance-preserving knowledge base with three planes: source evidence, reusable synthesis, and agent memory. Decision-aware retrieval assembles compact evidence packs, role-specific agents reason over them and invoke a simulator (Vidur or GAUSS) whenever quantitative support is needed, and every finding is written back as a scoped evidence record, so knowledge guides experiments and experiments refine knowledge. In configuration search over four serving scenarios, NoeVera comes within 5% of the optimum in a median of 6-7 simulator calls, versus 9 for Bayesian optimization and 15 for a knowledge-free agent with the same tools; on A100 GPUs, its representative configurations deliver ~1.30x vLLM-default throughput and meet every scenario's latency objective. When reused, provenance-preserving evidence records over-generalize on only 8% of applicability traps, versus 28% for a general-purpose agent memory. On the held-out 48-task split of a 72-task benchmark, NoeVera scores 29% higher than an equally equipped agent and 36% higher than its single-call retrieval counterpart (0.80 vs. 0.62 and 0.59), and even when baselines receive NoeVera's own prompts, a statistically significant part of its evidence-evolution advantage remains.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Exact k-nearest-neighbor vector search lies on the critical path of machine learning systems, from sparse attention in the latest large language models (LLMs) to long-context memories and training-data deduplication. Exhaustive GPU search scans the whole dataset for every query, while approximate indexes return inexact neighbors. Recent methods skip almost every vector with a cheap half-precision proof that it lies too far away, but only on one GPU that holds the whole dataset. Our insight is to keep only the short rows of these proofs in GPU memory and to fetch the few remaining full vectors from host memory. Our system, Zarc, answers Euclidean, cosine, inner-product, and filtered queries exactly under updates. On four H100 GPUs, it answers 10,000 exact queries over one billion vectors in 1.1 seconds instead of five minutes. On eleven open LLMs, it retrieves the exact top-10 attention keys 2.2x to 13.1x faster than exhaustive search. In sparse attention over one million tokens, it runs 3.1x faster than bf16 selection with FlashInfer, which misses the exact top-64 for most queries.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: DataRecycle: Trustworthy Distillation of Structured Data from Scattered Web Evidence
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce reporting bias, and hide inconsistencies. We present DataRecycle, an interactive system that helps transform scattered web evidence into structured tables of comparable numerical facts. Given a user's query or statement, DataRecycle decomposes it into entities and attributes, retrieves candidate evidence, and organizes scattered, potentially conflicting records in a table-based evidence view. To address key challenges in automated data distillation (i.e., incomplete retrieval, untraceable generation, sparse data distribution, and multi-source inconsistency), DataRecycle adopts an ontology-guided, top-down data acquisition strategy, visualizes the recorded lineage from retrieved snippets to extracted values, and aligns heterogeneous data across dimensions such as time, definition, and scale. We evaluate DataRecycle through module-level experiments, a usage scenario, and a user study, showing that the system helps users organize numerical web evidence into provenance-linked tables and inspect uncertainty and conflicting sources.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Access Paths for Efficient Ordering with Large Language Models
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: In this work, we present the \texttt{LLM ORDER BY} semantic operator as a logical abstraction and conduct a systematic study of its physical implementations. First, we propose several improvements to existing semantic sorting algorithms and introduce a semantic-aware external merge sort algorithm. Our extensive evaluation reveals that no single implementation offers universal optimality on all datasets. From our evaluations, we observe a general scaling relationship between sorting cost and the ordering quality for comparison-based algorithms. Building on these insights, we design a budget-aware optimizer that utilizes heuristic rules, LLM-as-Judge evaluation, and consensus aggregation to dynamically select the near-optimal access path for LLM ORDER BY. In our extensive evaluations, our optimizer consistently achieves ranking accuracy on par with or superior to the best static methods across all benchmarks. We believe that this work provides foundational insights into the principled optimization of semantic operators essential for building robust, large-scale LLM-powered analytic systems.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N agents observe distinct viewpoints, exchange budget-constrained natural language messages, and collaborate to enable a listener to answer spatial queries. We then introduce a novel multi-view spatial benchmark to isolate queries that demand non-trivial multi-view integration. Through an extensive empirical study, we discover that the penalty of restricting decentralized spatial reasoning to natural language with limited budget is far smaller than suggested by prior two-agent literature. Nevertheless, we observe that substantial headroom still remains for multi-agent spatial reasoning in this setting, as evidenced by a significant gap between current centralized performance and an oracle best-of-K ceiling. Moreover, we show that reinforcement learning with credit assignment substantially bolsters the decentralized model, effectively closing the gap with the centralized baseline.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Native-Space 3D CarveMix for Multi-Site T1w Stroke Segmentation
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Segmenting ischemic stroke lesions on T1-weighted (T1w) MRI acquired across different scanners and protocols without intensity standardization is difficult because lesions are subtle and share intensity characteristics with cerebrospinal fluid. Standard deep learning architectures trained across multiple centers plateau around Dice 0.66, with acute lesions ($\le 7$ days post-stroke) performing substantially worse due to severe sample scarcity. We combine a MedNeXt-L ($k=5$) backbone with on-the-fly 3D CarveMix augmentation that pastes real lesion patches into recipient training patches. By generating synthetic lesion placements dynamically within each fold with subject-level split isolation, the model sees more diverse lesion patterns without requiring pre-generated copies on disk. We evaluate on 1,453 native T1w scans from 55 clinical centers in the ISLES 2026 challenge. MedNeXt-L with CarveMix achieved a mean five-fold cross-validation Dice of 0.648 after 500 epochs. For comparison, the estimated Dice for plain MedNeXt-L at epoch 500 was 0.630, obtained by interpolation from its 1,000-epoch training trajectory.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at the SWITCH+ Workshop (ISLES 2026 Challenge), MICCAI 2026. Springer LNCS

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: In rateless transmission the transmitter keeps sending until the legitimate receiver (Bob) can decode. Over a wiretap channel this has a useful side effect: the eavesdropper (Eve) sees only as many symbols as Bob needs, although the transmitter knows neither channel. We study the secrecy of rateless lattice codes in this setting. First, using a public dither and privacy amplification, we prove a finite-length secrecy bound, in total variation distance, for every channel realization, even if Eve knows all codes and seeds and combines all packets. Second, stopping when Bob acknowledges successful decoding, as in hybrid ARQ, costs at most the logarithm of the number of possible feedback outcomes in secret bits. Third, for degraded sessions with state-based stopping and without a pre-shared key or other public discussion, the secret-key rate of a session cannot exceed its accumulated Gaussian secrecy capacity, and adaptive key generation with shaped rateless lattice codes comes within any $ε>0$ of this limit when Eve's channel states are revealed after the session. If only their statistics are known, choosing the key length after the session guarantees a prescribed secrecy-outage probability. Finally, over block Rayleigh fading with a CRC-based acknowledgement and joint belief-propagation decoding, and with Eve $20$~dB weaker on average, the scheme reaches $59$--$69\%$ of the outage-weighted throughput of an ideal infinite-length secure hybrid-ARQ benchmark for Bob SNRs of $8$--$20$~dB.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 1 table

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$π$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two simultaneous events in one monolithic scintillator and enables Compton camera devices with compact, monolithic scintillator volumes for enhanced portability.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Rate-Quality-Energy Convex Hull for High Dynamic Range Adaptive Video Streaming
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: High Dynamic Range (HDR) video introduces substantially higher decoding complexity and energy consumption than Standard Dynamic Range (SDR), yet most adaptive streaming pipelines still rely on bitrate ladders optimized using SDR-oriented metrics such as VMAF. These ladders fail to capture HDR-specific perceptual behavior and ignore decoder-side energy, resulting in energetically inefficient operating points. This work proposes a rate-quality-energy convex-hull optimization framework that jointly considers bitrate, HDR-aware perceptual quality (HDRVMAF), and client-side processing energy, including decoding and upscaling. Experiments on twelve 4K HDR sequences from the LIVE HDR Video Quality Assessment Database evaluate 72 representations per clip and demonstrate that traditional VMAF-optimized ladders frequently select high-resolution encodes that become dominated once energy is accounted for. Compared to the Default HLS ladder, our HDR-aware method achieves substantial bitrate savings of up to 54.34% at equal HDRVMAF, while yielding relative client-side energy reductions of up to 43.10% under higher energy weighting. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a practical foundation for constructing HDR bitrate ladders that explicitly expose and control perceptual quality-energy trade-offs.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Beyond File-Level Splits: Rethinking Symbolic Music Evaluation via Multi-View Alignment
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Symbolic music generation often continues MIDI passages by predicting subsequent notes or events. Held-out prediction loss can overestimate generalization to unseen compositions when training contains another performance or arrangement of a test work. We introduce Multi-View Alignment-Aware Same-Work Identification, combining complementary musical representations with temporal alignment of shared passages to remove test-work versions from training while preserving unrelated material and fixing evaluation files. In a controlled cohort of 100 manually verified pairs selected for high embedding similarity, replacing 3.29% of training windows with test-work versions reduces mean per-group NLL by up to 30.16% relative to matched unrelated content. Across two datasets and two generators, our method brings test losses closest to a reference built from independent work labels. Compared with removing the same number of files at random, it leaves fewer test works exposed and retains more eligible content, including about 99% of eligible tokens on the piano-performance dataset. A separate study on that dataset matches training tokens and updates: no test works remain exposed under the dataset labels, and mean relative test loss is 2.15% higher than an independently selected reference. These findings support keeping all versions of each composition in one split when evaluating generalization to unseen works. The project is available at https://kunbai05-nb.github.io/.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Routing Collapse in Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts: Cross-Modal Conditioning Restores Expert Diversity Without Improving Accuracy
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) classifiers are increasingly applied to multimodal emotion recognition, yet the health of their routing distributions is rarely measured. We study a seven-expert MoE head on IEMOCAP under two conditions that differ only in how modality embeddings are fused before reaching it: a learned scalar gate alone, and the same gate preceded by pairwise cross-modal attention. Under scalar fusion the router collapses, concentrating on 1.88 of seven experts at a normalised entropy of 0.241. Cross-modal fusion raises entropy to 0.537 and utilisation to 3.25 experts, a 2.23x increase (p=0.035, Cohen's d=2.55), and induces emotion-differentiated routing absent in the scalar case. This recovered diversity confers no detectable benefit: across six seeds per condition, weighted accuracy (p=0.646) and run-to-run variance (p=0.768) are statistically indistinguishable. We further observe a 13-point accuracy spread under identical configuration. In this regime, router health and task performance are decoupled, and diagnosing collapse does not by itself justify fixing it.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: SemGuard: Semantics-Decoupled Watermarking for Gaussian Splatting
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Gaussian Splatting provides an efficient representation for high-fidelity rendering of static and dynamic 3D scenes, motivating the copyright protection of Gaussian assets. In CLIP-guided Gaussian watermarking, a universal message decoder pretrained on textual watermark representations is subsequently applied to visual features containing both watermark information and scene-dependent semantics. However, text-only pretraining does not explicitly account for the semantic interference encountered during watermark extraction. To address this challenge, we propose SemGuard, a simple yet effective semantics-decoupled watermarking framework that learns to suppress scene-dependent semantic interference during universal message decoder pretraining. Specifically, SemGuard combines message-related CLIP text features with message-independent visual features extracted from unwatermarked scene images, constructing training representations with controllable semantic interference relevant to the target Gaussian assets. A progressive semantic interference curriculum gradually increases the contribution of visual features, allowing the decoder to first learn reliable message representations and then adapt to increasingly strong scene-dependent semantic interference. After pretraining for a given message length and semantic image pool, the decoder is frozen and reused across multiple Gaussian assets whose visual semantics are covered by the pretraining data. Experiments on static and dynamic Gaussian Splatting assets demonstrate improved rendering fidelity alongside reliable watermark extraction, while evaluations on static assets further show enhanced robustness against image-space distortions.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Multimedia (under review)

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: HME-PFD: Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Privileged Feature Distillation
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, facilitating efficient serving of machine learning systems. In the context of ads recommendation, privileged features distillation (PFD) extends KD by allowing the teacher model to leverage privileged features, i.e., features available only during training, to enhance distillation performance. However, in real-world scenarios, privileged features often have limited coverage and exhibit heterogeneous distributions, resulting in training examples of varying importance for distillation and model learning. We propose Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Privileged Feature Distillation (HME-PFD), a novel approach that incorporates privileged features into the routing module of a Mixture-of-Experts-based student model. Our method introduces both hard-coded and learnable routing modules, enabling the student to dynamically determine expert assignment based on the availability and values of privileged features. This design allows the student model to better handle the heterogeneous data scenario, where privileged features are partially observed, by differentiating between high- and low-signal samples. Extensive experiments on two post-click conversion prediction tasks demonstrate that HME-PFD consistently outperforms baseline methods. Our results show that leveraging privileged features for expert routing in the student model leads to improved model performance, even when privileged features are incomplete or sparse.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. We split rank-based compatibility by data availability and pair it with error correction and alert-list effects. We compared each update with ordinary retraining on the old inputs, predicting ICU admission or death and hospital admission, on 78,475 emergency department visits from MC-MED and, in a pre-registered replication, 100,000 stays from MIMIC-IV-ED at a second hospital. Radiograph report text gave no detectable gain and almost no extra re-ranking. Laboratory results improved prediction but, at both hospitals and with linear or tree models, pushed patients without labs down alert lists; linear updates also reshuffled them more than retraining did, without ranking them better. A top-20% admission list caught 4.2% of admitted patients without labs after the update, against 18.8% after retraining (second hospital: 4.9% against 22.6%), while catching more patients overall. This held for list sizes from 5% to 50% and in every patient group we checked, despite better measured calibration. Separate alert thresholds for patients with and without labs restored most or all of their catch rate at both hospitals at almost no cost. Teams should check these patients before deploying such an update.
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: Accepted at the 6th International Workshop on Multi-Modal Medical Data Analysis (MMMDA), IEEE BigData 2026

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: ChatGPT Can't Sell (And That's Probably a Good Thing): Buyer-Aligned AI Advice, the Sales-Representative Gap, and Evidence from Commercial Conversations
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: AI assistants and merchant sales agents have different objectives: assistants should help buyers compare options and preserve the choice not to purchase, while sales agents also guide qualified buyers toward an authorized next step. We study this sales-representative gap with three evidence streams. In 12,178 historical English GPT-family conversations screened for commercial or transactional intent, a 279-request sample contained recommendation language in 63 first replies (22.6%) and no narrow transactional action wording. In a 56-conversation explicit-buying sample, 24 replies (42.9%) contained recommendation markers, 32 (57.1%) qualification phrases, and none transaction-specific phrases. These lexical measures do not estimate successful selling. A 2026 brand-monitoring cohort of 1,050 GPT-5.4--Gemini answer pairs over 383 purchase-related prompts showed transaction-specific phrases in 0.0% of recommendation-worded prompts, 0.21% of price/comparison prompts, and 9.52% of explicitly transaction-worded prompts. The prompts are selected, not organic shopping sessions. In a prospective pilot across five matched hypothetical product scenarios, sales instructions produced more next-step language than general-assistant instructions (5/5 vs. 2/5), but no increase in clean product choice (3/5 in both); unsupported offers and fit errors also occurred. This pilot cannot establish a population effect. A separate company-affiliated randomized field study reports higher engaged-visitor conversion for Javo, a commercially trained sales agent, than for a frontier-model agent in shared tooling, but does not identify the mechanism. We argue that apparent reluctance to sell can be appropriate for buyer-aligned assistants. Merchant agents should optimize qualified decision progress through catalog grounding, truthful authorization, and safeguards against unsuitable sales.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: A Study of Prior Case Retrieval Using Lexical, Semantic, and Rhetorical Role Information in Indian Legal Documents
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: For retrieving prior cases in Indian legal judgments, the problem involves distinguishing relevant legal facts from mere lexical similarities because a prior case that shares a statute with the query judgment is not necessarily relevant. In this paper, we describe an empirical evaluation of three consecutive designs of retrieval systems for the IL PCR(Indian Legal Prior Case Retrieval) task. We demonstrate that the combination of the rhetorical roles (Fact, Ratio Of The Decision, Precedent, Argument, Statute) is better than either using individual roles or performing full text retrieval, that statute similarity is not discriminative, and that a legal entailment reranker with training data produced by an LLM is much worse in terms of official evaluation than its internal validation score. Two rankers, with excellent internal MRR up to 0.97, performed poorly in terms of official evaluation (MRR as low as 0.14). Thus, we propose a new design with query disjoint splitting and frozen validation fusion. The result is a four stage pipeline with Micro F1 0.2549, MRR 0.6081, and nDCG@10 0.4187.

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: An assistant that brings up memories unasked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. This decision is a multiple-testing problem whose difficulty grows with store size N. On replays of LongMemEval, a similarity threshold tuned to 5% false alarms at N=8 reaches 84-100% at N=2048 across embedding models and cue types; LoCoMo and LLM judges show it too. We prove that a gate which thresholds the best of N independent irrelevant scores at false-alarm rate alpha works at a per-item false-positive rate of about -ln(1-alpha)/N, which pins its hit rate to the far left of the ROC and makes it regularly varying in N under regular variation. If the relevant memory is equally likely to be any of the N, whatever a gate reads and however it decides, at false-alarm rate alpha it hits at most alpha+sqrt(alpha(1-alpha)chi^2/N), with chi^2 the divergence between a relevant and an irrelevant memory, and with equal-variance binormal scores the best-score gate is optimal. At matched false alarms the deployed score recalls 14-26 points more than raw cosine. A cue-swap conformal gate, which ranks the current cue among other cues on the store, has a finite-sample false-alarm guarantee under exchangeability. With the user's unfiltered history as background it keeps false alarms at 3-6% on LongMemEval at the hit rate of a label-tuned threshold; on LoCoMo it overshoots or turns conservative depending on the source of its reference cues. In a chronological replay with the user's earlier messages as references, it fires on 5-8% of questions on stores without their answer and on 6-8% of session-opening turns, against 57% for the deployed gate at N=2048. A cross-encoder pays the same price, and on a prospective-memory benchmark similarity gates recall at most 9% of constraints at controlled false alarms. Code and data: https://github.com/RiverChenStillCompiling/price-of-scale
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.comment: v4: adds a bound for every gate, including judges that read every memory, and shows that the best-score gate is optimal for equal-variance binormal scores; restates the mechanism claim; 24 pages, 4 figures

Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.title: MMIntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu
Information Retrieval / RAG / Search.summary: Multimodal search with image-text queries helps users find notes in user-generated content (UGC) communities and serves as a key search tool for multimodal search agents. For such queries, query-note relevance depends on the user's retrieval intent and cannot be determined by visual or topical similarity alone. Simply reranking visual search results cannot fully address this challenge, as notes relevant to the user's intent may be missing from the initial candidate set. This motivates explicit intent modeling to align candidate retrieval and reranking under consistent relevance criteria. We present MMIntentFlow, an intent-driven real-time multimodal search system deployed at Xiaohongshu over an index on the order of ten billion entries. MMIntentFlow represents retrieval objectives with a hierarchical intent taxonomy and uses intent-specific relevance criteria to guide data construction, representation learning, and reranking. An offline agentic data workflow acquires candidates and verifies their relevance under these criteria to produce training supervision. The embedding model combines intent-aware contrastive learning, graded ranking, and distribution distillation, while a compact reranker assesses query-candidate evidence conditioned on predicted hierarchical intents.
