Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: We present Kandinsky 6.0 Video, a family of foundation diffusion models for synchronized text-to-audio-video generation, comprising Kandinsky 6.0 Video Lite (3B parameters) and Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro (29B parameters). Both models generate 5-second video clips with synchronized 44 kHz audio, including lip-sync, in text-to-audio-video (T2AV) and image-to-audio-video (I2AV) modes; a built-in super-resolution model raises the output resolution to Full-HD (1920x1080). Building on the video generation capabilities of Kandinsky 5.0, Kandinsky 6.0 Video employs a dual-stream CrossDiT architecture that connects a pretrained video stream and a newly trained audio stream through bidirectional cross-attention for temporal and semantic alignment. Our continuous pretraining strategy first trains the audio stream from scratch on large-scale audio corpora and then trains both streams jointly on paired audio-video data while preserving unimodal fidelity; pretraining is followed by supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement-learning-based post-training, and distillation. In side-by-side human evaluation, Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro clearly outperforms its predecessor, Kandinsky 5.0 Video Pro, and remains competitive with leading audio-video generation models, outperforming LTX 2.5 and Seedance 2.0 in speech quality. To accelerate open research and deployment in multimedia generation, we release the code, model checkpoints, and diffusers integration under the MIT license.
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Technical report on the open-source T2AV model. GitHub: https://github.com/kandinskylab/kandinsky-6

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. Among judgments of retained emotionaldevelopment content, narrative choices account for 60.0% and scenario operation for 7.2%. These findings identify two linked priorities for film-to-game adaptation: preserving source situations that can support gameplay and connecting retained content to player actions and consequences.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Learning Binary Codes with Spiking Neural Networks for Cross-Modal Hashing Retrieval
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Cross-modal hashing (CMH) uses compact binary codes for efficient image-text retrieval. Most methods learn image-text relationships in a continuous space and binarize the representation only at the end. Semantic learning and bit decisions thus remain largely separate. This work addresses two key questions concerning hash-bit generation: \textbf{(1) How to determine hash bits?} We leverage the discrete nature of spiking activity and determine each bit through competition between positive and negative spikes accumulated over time, rather than through a single firing event or subsequent thresholding of continuous representations. \textbf{(2) How to generate such hash bits?} We propose an unsupervised spiking framework for cross-modal hashing, in which image and text jointly contribute to hash-bit generation through temporal interaction. An activation constraint further prevents unsupported decisions caused by silent channel pairs. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and support temporal spike competition as a design principle for hash-code generation.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets. Across eight terrestrial, optical, and sonar benchmarks, multi-step lookahead outperforms static schedules and search-free offline RL under tight budgets -- gaining up to 28.4 AP percentage points over static priority on RUOD and 15.1 on ARIS -- while dynamic pricing lifts large-budget performance on all eight domains at 11 ms planning cost. Ultimately, pairing lightweight learned dynamics with exact symbolic constraints turns frozen detectors into adaptive, budget-aware inspection agents without retraining.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate opportunities for interaction into better understanding. We introduce VideoACE, a benchmark for assessing video understanding under conditions that support sustained interaction. We focus on high-frame-rate action videos, where rapid, subtle changes make targeted observation especially valuable. The benchmark comprises 1,000 multiple-choice questions spanning six categories of fine-grained action understanding, accompanied by temporal evidence annotations and user hints screened for answer leakage. Its evaluation environment combines video inspection tools with a user simulator, allowing models to adjust temporal coverage, sampling density, and spatial detail, and to revisit evidence and revise their judgments under simulated user feedback. We evaluate single-pass observation, autonomous tool use, and tool use combined with user feedback to examine how effectively models exploit these opportunities. Evaluation of five models reveals distinct patterns in how they acquire evidence and respond to opportunities for further interaction. These findings establish VideoACE as a testbed for examining agentic video understanding beyond performance under a fixed observation setting.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Facial Action Unit Detection Based on Multi-task Learning Strategy for Unlabeled Facial Images in the Wild
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Facial Action Unit (AU) detection often relies on highly-cost accurate labeling or inaccurate pseudo labeling techniques in recent years. How to introduce large amounts of unlabeled facial images in the wild into supervised AU detection frameworks has become a challenging problem. Additionally, nearly every type of AUs has the problem of unbalanced positive and negative samples. Inspired by other multi-task learning frameworks, we first propose a multi-task learning strategy boosting AU detection in the wild through jointing facial landmark detection and AU domain separation and reconstruction. Our introduced dual domains facial landmark detection framework can solve the lack of accurate facial landmark coordinates during the AU domain separation and reconstruction training process, while the parameters of homostructural facial extraction modules from these two similar facial tasks are shared. Moreover, we propose a pixel-level feature alignment scheme to maintain the consistency of features obtained from two separation and reconstruction processes. Furthermore, a weighted asymmetric loss is proposed to change the contribution of positive and negative samples of each type of AUs to model parameters updating. Experimental results on three widely used benchmarks demonstrate our superiority to most state-of-the-art methods for AU detection.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Auditing Hyperstimulation at Scale in Child-Facing YouTube Videos
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Parents, pediatricians, and journalists have raised concern that child-facing videos are becoming increasingly stimulating (faster-paced, louder, and more visually dense), but this concern rests mostly on ad hoc observation rather than systematic measurement. We present a large-scale audit of hyperstimulation patterns, which we refer to as content-independent production choices, such as rapid cutting, that may place demands on children's developing cognitive and sensory processing capacities. Drawing on parents' Reddit discussions and developmental psychology, we develop computational metrics for 12 hyperstimulation patterns. We apply these metrics to 16,375 videos from 542 child-facing YouTube channels spanning 2015-2026. We found broad increases in stimulation over time, with cut rates rising across all five content categories. Nearly a quarter of the channels increased in at least one stimulation pattern over time. More stimulating videos also tended to receive more views, but the relevant stimulation patterns differed across content types.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: FLARE: Full-Modality Long-Video Audiovisual Retrieval Benchmark with User-Simulated Queries
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: As video becomes increasingly central to information dissemination and multimodal large language models (MLLMs) continue to advance, evaluating video retrieval has become increasingly important. In realistic search scenarios, this requires matching short user queries to long-form content using both visual and auditory evidence. Yet existing retrieval benchmarks are still dominated by short clips, single modalities, and caption-based evaluation. We introduce FLARE, a full-modality long-video audiovisual retrieval benchmark with user-simulated queries. Built from 399 carefully screened Video-MME videos (10--60 min, 225.4 h) to ensure source quality and diversity, FLARE contains 87,697 clips annotated with vision, audio, and unified audiovisual captions, together with 274,933 user-style queries. Cross-modal queries are further filtered by a hard bimodal constraint, requiring retrieval to fail under either modality alone but succeed when both are combined. FLARE evaluates models under two regimes, caption-based and query-based retrieval, across vision, audio, and unified audiovisual settings. Experiments with 15 representative retrievers show that user-style queries substantially change model behavior, strong caption-based performance does not always transfer to query-based retrieval, and audio--language alignment remains a key bottleneck for unified audiovisual retrieval. Our code and data are released at https://flarebench.github.io/

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: Animating virtual opponents is an important yet challenging task in game development. In martial arts games, opponent motions must not only be physically plausible but also exhibit appropriate technique, timing, transitions, and target-directed intent. Traditional game animations often rely on handcrafted clips, state machine transitions, and procedural adjustments, which can be labor-intensive and may limit the behavioral diversity of non-player characters. This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework for character animation in virtual sparring games. Inspired by Tang Soo Do, we collected a martial arts motion capture dataset containing isolated attacking and defending techniques, technique combinations and transitions, and contextual sparring variations. We first pretrained a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from the captured data using reinforcement learning (RL) with adversarial style rewards, and then adapted these skills with task-specific rewards for target-directed striking and threat-aware evasion. We evaluated the motions generated by the learned policy through a user study, in which participants assessed their physical plausibility, smoothness, and martial arts form. To demonstrate their applicability to interactive gameplay, we developed a VR sparring prototype for Meta Quest headsets. The prototype combines policy-generated motion clips with lightweight state-based control to support interactive opponent behavior. Together, these findings support the feasibility of using a learned martial arts skill repertoire as a motion foundation for animating opponents in VR sparring games.

Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.title: Lifting 3D Gaussians: A Wavelet Multiresolution Representation for Scalable Gaussian Splatting Streaming
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) represents a scene as an unstructured set of primitives optimized at a single scale, offering no native support for progressive delivery to heterogeneous devices. Existing scalable approaches organize these primitives into independent quality layers or spatial hierarchies. However, maintaining separate splat representations across scales introduces redundancy, while independent layers have limited ability to correct coarse geometry as finer detail arrives. We present LiftGS, a multiresolution representation that organizes a scene into a coarse Gaussian set and a tree of refinements. Each refinement replaces one coarse Gaussian with two finer children whose attributes are learned relative to their parent. Inspired by wavelet lifting, we encode these changes using a shared detail vector and per-attribute factors that allow the two children to differ asymmetrically from the parent. A client first receives the coarse set, then reconstructs and substitutes children as refinement data arrives. This construction reuses previously transmitted attributes to encode finer detail and removes replaced parents from the active rendering set, reducing both refinement payload and rendering memory. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets show LiftGS cuts splat redundancy from over 65% to under 25%, reduces transmission payload and GPU memory by up to 2.4x and 5.5x over state-of-the-art scalable-3DGS baselines, achieves smooth quality transitions in simulated progressive delivery, and compresses a further 8.7x with standard coding at negligible quality loss. Project website: https://yuang-ian.github.io/liftgs/
Multimodal / Vision-Language / VLM.comment: Accepted by MMSys'27; Project page: https://yuang-ian.github.io/liftgs/

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Mammography Foundation Models for Opportunistic Prediction of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death among women, yet cardiovascular risk assessment often relies on clinical variables that may be missing, outdated, or unavailable in routine care. Screening mammography offers an opportunity for opportunistic cardiovascular risk stratification because it is routinely acquired and contains vascular features, including breast arterial calcifications (BAC), that are associated with cardiovascular risk and events. We evaluate whether mammography specific foundation models, originally pretrained for breast cancer related tasks, can transfer to cardiovascular risk prediction without cardiovascular specific supervision or explicit BAC annotation. We constructed a 5-year major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) cohort of 22,497 women linked to electronic health record outcomes, including 500 events (2.22% prevalence).Using only the screening mammogram, the foundation models achieved AUROCs of 0.823 and 0.822, recovering most of the gain of a clinical risk factor model (AUROC 0.859) over an age-only model (0.765), without requiring any clinical variables. Both foundation models evaluated assigned substantially higher predicted risk to patients with radiologist documented BAC, despite BAC never being used as a training label, and showed activation patterns consistent with vascular findings. Together, these findings suggest that mammography foundation models can recover clinically relevant cardiovascular risk information directly from mammographic pixels and suggest that screening mammography may provide an opportunistic source of cardiovascular risk information to complement conventional clinical assessment without additional imaging.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: Accepted at ML4H 2026

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model. A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations, so that 69 of its 2048 features are named after Gleason morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis. The same code feeds a grading network, which reads all features to predict Gleason patterns and the Grade Group, while morphology maps read directly from the named features. We evaluate the system on five public datasets that include needle biopsies, tissue-microarray cores, multi-reader annotations, and three scanners. The morphology maps remain stable across alignment runs and, without retraining, detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores when evaluated by up to six pathologists (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919). In an independent biopsy cohort, Grade Group agreement with three pathologists on Leica scans is close to their agreement with each other. Removing the named features reduces the corresponding Gleason pattern predictions by 49% to 98%, with effects larger than those from 20 activity-matched random feature removals. These results show that a shared sparse representation can support competitive Gleason grading while providing named morphological evidence that transfers across datasets and whose contribution to grading can be measured directly.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Stochastic Optimisation for Scalable Ptychographic Image Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: X-ray ptychography is a lensless coherent diffraction imaging technique capable of high spatial resolution, in which an image is reconstructed by solving a large-scale inverse problem from highly redundant far-field diffraction measurements acquired under overlapping illumination. Whilst the measurement redundancy created by overlapping illumination is essential for reconstruction fidelity, it leads to computational and memory demands that scale poorly with object size and target resolution when using conventional reconstruction algorithms. This work proposes a ptychographic reconstruction framework that reduces peak memory usage and time to convergence by leveraging stochastic optimisation techniques developed for large-scale machine learning. Specifically, the framework employs stochastic gradient descent with a decaying step size that progressively reduces the effect of gradient noise, referred to here as variance reduction (VR), with gradients that agree with automatic differentiation, to optimise the ptychographic forward model using randomly sampled subsets of diffraction measurements. For an experimental dataset of 200,000 diffraction patterns of $128\times128$ pixels, VR is demonstrated to require $65\%$ of the peak GPU memory and $22\%$ of the reconstruction time of the established maximum-likelihood (ML) algorithm. The VR framework incorporates the Poisson maximum-likelihood formulation and partial coherence within a unified and extensible optimisation setting. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves reconstruction quality visually comparable to established methods, with lower peak GPU memory and a shorter time
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 38 pages, 12 figures

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Micrograph B-factor estimation via Wilson statistics
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: The single-particle cryo-electron microscopy imaging process is known to cause exponential decay in the amplitude and power spectra of proteins. This decay is modeled by the B factor and is currently corrected as a post-processing stage of the 3D reconstruction. As a consequence, all experimental images in the dataset are assumed to share the same B factor. In this paper, we suggest a novel approach wherein the B factor is determined and corrected as a preprocessing step to the reconstruction. We show such an approach can improve reconstruction resolution.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Separating Module Gain From Transport Plan Contribution in Audio-Visual Dynamic Facial Expression Recognition
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: A cross-modal routing module can improve over its backbone while its transport plan accounts for no demonstrable part of that improvement. In ABVnet with DFEW, Sinkhorn cross-modal routing (SCR) exceeds the retrained baseline by 0.87 unweighted average recall (UAR) points, a resolved difference, yet sits 0.17 points above an individually trained, parameter-matched pooled variant, an unresolved difference that establishes no equivalence; under the development protocol the comparison with the baseline reverses. Separating the two needs comparisons a module-against-backbone test cannot supply: parameter-matched variants changing only the plan rule, and interventions replacing the plan without retraining. The evaluation covers MMA-DFER and ABVnet on DFEW and MAFW, and MMA-DFER on CREMA-D, with a single training run per configuration and paired fold intervals. ABVnet with DFEW motivated the follow-up after the broader results were available. Replacing the plan everywhere with a uniform one reduces UAR by 0.72, whereas permuting its rows gives an unresolved difference of -0.20 UAR points; permutation is less damaging by 0.51 UAR points, a resolved contrast. Replacing the plan with the product of its own marginals, preserving both marginals and removing only frame-specific mixtures, reduces UAR by 0.70. These reductions concern reliance at inference; attribution of the module gain to the transport plan remains unestablished. Under the 1.5 fold-dependence widening, the baseline gain remains resolved, whereas the replacement reductions and the paired contrast are unresolved.

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Decoding Motion-Blurred QR Codes: Motion-Parameter Error Tolerance and Model-Based Recovery
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: In automated manufacturing, logistics, and inspection, Quick Response (QR) codes are often read on the fly under continuous ambient light without active strobes or motion pauses. The resulting relative three-dimensional motion produces spatially varying blur that defeats standard decoders, yet how accurately the motion must be estimated to recover the payload remains an open question. To address this question from a task-driven evaluation perspective centered on machine recognition effectiveness, we formulate motion-blurred QR recovery within a unified mathematical framework of identifiability. Within this framework, we systematically measure the decoding tolerance to perturbations in motion length, direction, rotation or scaling centre, and speed profile. These controlled experiments reveal three structural laws: 1) parameter tolerances shrink rapidly as blur amplitude grows and are tightest under uniform speed, whereas accelerating motion is substantially more forgiving; 2) length tolerance can differ markedly between underestimation and overestimation; 3) errors that are individually benign interact strongly and prevent decoding when combined. Guided by these findings, we propose a grey-box recovery pipeline in which two compact networks predict an initial corner trajectory, followed by tolerance-guided candidate search, alternating image-and-path fitting, and regularised linear inversion. On a benchmark of 955 real motion-blurred photographs spanning four camera models and four rigid-motion families, our method recovers the exact payload on 93.1% of the images. It outperforms the strongest fine-tuned deblurring network at 83.6% and reduces the decoding error rate by 58.0%, with zero wrong strings accepted.
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, and 11-page double-column supplementary material. v3: updated Fig. 5 visual comparison (four motion categories), aligned with the IEEE TCI submission

Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.title: Temporal Persistence for Stylized Rendering: Historical Image Storage and Reconstruction
Image Processing / OCR Preprocessing.summary: The overlapping silhouettes and gradual fading in The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (released April 27, 2000) produce a distinctive depiction of motion blur, in which earlier scene states remain visible as part of the current image. Reproducing this appearance in a modern renderer involves decisions about when historical images are sampled, how their contributions are retained, and how the resulting history can be represented within the available memory and processing budget. In this paper, we investigate these decisions through complete image histories, shared image regions, and selectively retained pixel changes, using Godot engine implementations evaluated against independently composited references. For a ten-image history sampled at 20 Hz on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, half-float storage halves history allocation and reduces median storage-pass duration by factors of 2.40 at 720p and 1.73 at 1080p, preserving the supplied source precision. The adaptive experiments examine how memory savings depend on reconstruction metadata and allocation, including a sparse representation that reduces allocation by 83.81% at low resolution with 445.25 times the GPU duration.
